area: SCAN experience (live feed, grouping, filters, row actions, band tagging, last-heard strip, record toggle, counters, send-to-Lab)
summary: iOS has the skeleton of the Android Scan tab (GROUPED/RAW, the same 8 sections, CLASS filter, collapsible headers, show-control toggle, log toggle, compact band strip), but most of what makes it usable is missing or broken. Row swipe actions never fire because the rows are not in a List, so nothing can be deleted, added to TX, or sent to the Lab from the scan feed. The strip never shows the iPhone's own scan and has no light-effect filter. Nothing the iPhone hears is saved, there is no band-address tagging, and the log is 3 columns against Android's 13. The iOS classifier also disagrees with Android on common packets: Android's own built-in colour presets are dropped by the default iOS filter, and ping-prefixed effects collapse into one "Interaction Ping" row. The Android strip fix (lastLightHex / lightsBand) is an uncommitted working-tree change that was live while I read; iOS needs the same rule.

gaps.title: Last-lights strip: follow only light effects, and follow the iPhone's own scan
gaps.androidBehaviour: ScanTab pins LastHeardStrip(state.lastLightHex, state.lightsHeard). handleHeard updates lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard only when BandEffectModel.from(hex).lightsBand is true (kind is not NONE, PING or WAND), so pings, beacons and wand colours never replace the last real effect. Title is "LAST LIGHTS · #<lightsHeard>", empty text "LAST LIGHTS · NONE HEARD YET". statusJson also exports the three fields. This is an uncommitted working-tree change.
gaps.iosState: LastHeardStrip takes the newest of vm.livePackets and vm.androidLivePackets with no kind filter. vm.livePackets is only filled when isRecording, and only the unreferenced RecordTab toggles that, so the iPhone's own feed (vm.iscanRawLive) never reaches the strip. With an ESP32 relay or no relay it stays on "NOTHING YET". When the Android relay feed drives it, it shows whatever arrived last, including pings (dim face). Title shows buffer size ("N LIVE"), not a heard counter. BandEffectModel has no lightsBand; AndroidRemoteStatus.parse ignores lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: (1) BandEffectModel.swift: add `var lightsBand: Bool { kind != .none && kind != .ping && kind != .wand }`. (2) AppViewModel: add @Published lastLightHex, lastLightLabel, lightsHeard; set them in handlePacket when BandEffectModel.from(hex).lightsBand. Compute this before the line-188 filter until the filter is ported, because that filter currently drops real effects. Do not reset on clear (Android clearLive does not). (3) AndroidRemoteStatus: add and parse lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard. (4) Rewrite LastHeardStrip to read vm.lastLightHex / lightsHeard when isLocalListening, else androidRemote's fields; use Android's title and empty text; drop the vm.livePackets dependency. (5) RemoteScanView.statsBlock LAST row should show the light packet. About 60 lines.

gaps.title: Swipe actions on scan rows never fire (delete, TX/TAG), and there is no delete confirmation
gaps.androidBehaviour: Each row is a SwipePacketRow inside a LazyColumn. Swipe left opens ConfirmDeleteDialog ("Remove raw packet?" or "Remove from scan list?", with label and hex), then calls ServiceState.removeRawLive(timestampMs, hex) or removeLive(dedupeKey). Swipe right opens the "Packet action" dialog: ADD TO TX (store.saveCustomPreset) or RECATEGORIZE. Hint: "TAP REPLAY · HOLD MENU · SWIPE ← DEL · SWIPE → TX/TAG".
gaps.iosState: SwipeRemotePacketRow attaches .swipeActions, but both feeds are ForEach rows in a VStack inside a ScrollView. SwiftUI swipeActions only work on List rows, so neither swipe can be triggered. That makes the promote alert (Add to TX / Load Lab) and removeIscanUnique / removeIscanRaw / removeAndroid*Live unreachable from the UI. The hint text has the directions reversed against the code (leading edge is TX/TAG, trailing is Delete) and omits HOLD MENU. There is no confirm dialog. The VStack is also not lazy, so up to 200 local plus 120 relay rows rebuild on every packet.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Render the results in a List (Section per LivePacketSection, .listStyle(.plain), .scrollContentBackground(.hidden), .listRowBackground(MMTheme.navy), custom listRowInsets) so swipeActions work, or use LazyVStack with a custom DragGesture row. Add @State deleteRequest (packet, raw) and an alert showing label and hex before removing; set allowsFullSwipe false on delete. Fix the hint to "TAP REPLAY · HOLD MENU · SWIPE ← DEL · SWIPE → TX/TAG". Make removeIscanUnique also purge iscanRawLive (see drift).

gaps.title: Long-press packet action sheet
gaps.androidBehaviour: Long press opens PacketActionSheet (ModalBottomSheet): label, hex, "COLORS: …" from MagicClassifier.classify(hex).colors, subtitle "<CATEGORY> · RSSI n". Actions: Transmit, Load in Lab, Add to TX library, Recategorize, Remove (destructive, goes to the confirm dialog).
gaps.iosState: None. RemotePacketRow is a plain Button with no long-press or contextMenu on scan rows. The classified colours and category are never shown for a heard packet.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: New PacketActionSheet view (sheet with .presentationDetents([.medium])) plus a PacketAction struct {label, destructive, action}. Add an onLongPress parameter to SwipeRemotePacketRow / RemotePacketRow (.onLongPressGesture or .contextMenu). Add @State actionTarget in ISCanView and RemoteScanView. Header: label, hex, COLORS from MagicClassifier.classify(hex)?.colors, "\(category.rawValue) · RSSI \(rssi)". Actions map to vm.transmitAndroidHex, load-in-Lab, vm.saveAndroidCustomPreset, recategorize, remove with confirm.

gaps.title: Recategorize a heard packet (CategoryPickerDialog)
gaps.androidBehaviour: From the swipe-right dialog or the action sheet: pick SHOW / ANIMATION / COLOR / UNKNOWN. It calls store.saveCustomPreset(label.ifEmpty{category.name}, hex), then store.recategorizePacket(id, category) on the first allTransmitPackets() entry with the same canonical hex. Stored as MagicPacket.category in presets / learned lists in magicmaker_store.json. RenameDialog is defined in the same file but ScanTab does not use it (used by Logs at 962 and TX at 1879).
gaps.iosState: No category picker. The promote alert only offers Add to TX and Load Lab. RelayCommands.execute has no recategorize (or rename) action, and iOS MagicStore has neither recategorizePacket nor saveCustomPreset.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: A category picker (confirmationDialog over MagicCategory.allCases) reachable from the promote alert and the action sheet. Persistence, one of: (a) local — add saveCustomPreset(label:hex:) and recategorizePacket(id:category:) to iOS MagicStore and have the TX tab read the local library; or (b) relay — new action recategorize_packet {hex, category} in RelayCommands.kt, Handlers and the service (calls store.saveCustomPreset then recategorizePacket), plus vm.recategorizeAndroidPacket(hex:category:). Depends on what the library area decides.

gaps.title: Heard packets are never learned or saved on the iPhone
gaps.androidBehaviour: handleHeard calls store.processHeardPacket(hex, rssi, recordSession, address, lat, lng, accuracy) for every packet that passes the filter. Classified packets go to the library (Starlight to learnedColors with serial capture; colours; show/animation per distinct hex). Pings are never saved. Unclassified packets go to learnedRaw unless isLibraryNoise (8301C0…, 83010F11…, 8301CC03…) or the 20000 cap; telemetry from a tagged band is whitelisted. Returns RecordEvent.reason ("Learned X → Colors"), appends to recordings and the session CSV, and triggers cloudSync on a newly learned known packet.
gaps.iosState: handlePacket returns right after appendLocalLivePacket when isLocalListening, which is always true after launch (bootstrapAfterLaunch). store.processHeardPacket exists but is never reached, so nothing the iPhone hears is saved anywhere. The only way to keep a packet is Add to TX via the Android relay, which is unreachable (swipe gap). iOS MagicStore.hearRawPacket never saves raw packets and has no ping skip, noise filter, hex index or cap. The TX tab only reads androidCatalog.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Call store.processHeardPacket from the local-listening branch of handlePacket. Port into iOS MagicStore: ping skip in addClassifiedToLibrary, MagicClassifier.isLibraryNoise, raw learning with a Set<String> hex index, the 20000 cap and a 2.5 s coalesced save, per-distinct-hex dedupe for show/animation, and allowNoise for tagged bands. Show event.reason as the row note. Surface the iOS-local library in the TX tab next to the relay catalog. Overlaps the library area.

gaps.title: Strict show-control filter and TLV-based classification not ported (root cause of the drift below)
gaps.androidBehaviour: The SHOW-CTRL chip (default on, pref show_control_only) drops a packet in handleHeard unless MagicClassifier.isShowControl(hex): starts with 8301CC03, contains CF9B/CF0B, has an E9 record anywhere in the TLV chain (DisneyTlv.parse), or is a known show block. Classification walks the TLV chain: a ping is only a CC record with no E9 after it; an E9 record is an effect with or without a channel marker or ping prefix; EA/EF/E4/E5 beacon families get labels but are not show control.
gaps.iosState: The toggle exists and persists (UserDefaults iscan_show_control_only, default true), but the predicate is `MagicClassifier.classify(hex) == nil`. The iOS classifier is the old substring version: any 8301CC03… prefix is a ping even when an effect follows, and an effect needs the E?00E9 regex. There is no isShowControl, isLibraryNoise, classifyEffectFamily or pingName. The only TLV walk on iOS is private to BandEffectModel.records.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Port DisneyTlv.parse (Record / Parsed with first, has, effect) to Swift; BandEffectModel.records can be promoted to a shared type. Add MagicClassifier.isShowControl and isLibraryNoise. Change line 188 to `iscanShowControlOnly && !MagicClassifier.isShowControl(hex)`. In classify: ping only when there is no E9 record; classify E9 by record rather than regex; add classifyEffectFamily and the pingName labels. Decide whether PresetCatalog.showBlocks on iOS should shrink to Android's two entries.

gaps.title: Band-address tagging ("My MagicBand") plus address and BAND on each row
gaps.androidBehaviour: BleScanner reports result.device.address with every packet. LivePacket carries address and isBand; liveSubtitle renders "RSSI n · <address> · BAND | <note>" and the row is tinted when isBand. BandConfigSection (collapsed state persisted as band_menu_collapsed, default collapsed) lists tagged addresses with REMOVE, a manual MAC field with ADD, "SAVED BAND PACKETS: n" with DELETE ALL (confirm, store.deleteSavedBands), and "HEARD (TAP TO TAG)": the 8 most recent of UiState.seenAddresses (address, rssi, count; cap 80) with TAG/UNTAG. Storage: SharedPreferences "magicmaker" key band_addresses, comma-joined uppercase. A tagged address whitelists that band's telemetry into learnedRaw, sets is_band in the log and feeds the _band.csv sidecar.
gaps.iosState: No source identity anywhere. BleCentralDelegate.bleCentral(didReceive:rssi:) passes only hex and rssi; IScanLivePacket has no address or isBand; there is no seen-address list, band storage or UI. Row subtitle is "RSSI n · TAP → ANDROID TX". The Android-relay rows cannot show it either, because LivePacketDto omits address and isBand.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: CoreBluetooth hides the MAC, so use CBPeripheral.identifier.uuidString as the address. It rotates with the band's private address, the same caveat Android documents. Plumb it through BleCentralDelegate, BleCoordinator.onPacket and AppViewModel.handlePacket; add address and isBand to IScanLivePacket. Add a SeenAddress struct {address, rssi, lastSeenMs, count} and @Published seenAddresses (cap 80, newest first). Store UserDefaults band_addresses (comma-joined uppercase) with bandAddresses / isBandAddress / addBandAddress / removeBandAddress. New BandConfigSection view in ISCanView controls: collapsible, persisted band_menu_collapsed default true, tagged list with REMOVE, HEARD list (first 8) with TAG/UNTAG, a paste-identifier field in place of the MAC field. Subtitle "RSSI n · <id> · BAND" and a tinted row. "SAVED BAND PACKETS / DELETE ALL" depends on the auto-learn gap. Typing a real MAC is not possible on iOS.

gaps.title: Load in Lab from a scan row carries the label and jumps to the Lab tab
gaps.androidBehaviour: onLoadInLab(hex, label) calls store.saveLabHex(canonical) and saveLabLabel(label), then ServiceState.requestLabLoad() (labLoadTick++, so the Lab reloads) and sets tab = Lab. Offered in the long-press sheet.
gaps.iosState: "Load Lab" exists only in the swipe promote alert, which is unreachable. It calls vm.loadAndroidLabHex(hex), which sets androidLabHex only: no label, and the user stays on SCAN because the selected tab is private @State in ContentView.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Move the selected tab into RemoteUIState (or pass an onLoadInLab closure) so the scan views can switch to .lab. Change to loadAndroidLabHex(_ hex:, label:) and keep the label (add androidLabLabel to the VM if the Lab should show it). Call it from the action sheet and the promote alert.

gaps.title: Scan log format: 13-column session CSV with band and unique sidecars
gaps.androidBehaviour: LOG / LOG:ON toggles store.beginScanSession() / endScanSession(); logging is forced on whenever scanning is on. File scan_yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss.csv, header timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note,source_address,is_band,lat,lng,accuracy. Sidecar scan_<stamp>_band.csv holds rows from tagged bands; scan_<stamp>_unique.csv (hex,count,first_ms,last_ms,label,category,addresses) is written at session end. Rows are GPS-stamped from startLocationUpdates. Every advert that passes the filter is logged.
gaps.iosState: "Backup Log" writes Documents/iscan_backup/iscan_<ISO8601>.csv with header timestamp_ms,hex,rssi only: no label, category, type, colours, note, source, is_band or GPS, and no _band or _unique sidecars. Rows are also thinned by the 1.5 s radio dedupe in BleCentral, so the log cannot reproduce packet timing. MagicStore.beginScanSession (8 columns) exists but is only reachable through the dead isRecording path.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Make ISCanBackupLogger write Android's SESSION_HEADER and rows: classified label / category / typeInfo / colours, RecordEvent.reason as note, source id, is_band, lat / lng / accuracy (empty when unknown), with commas and newlines stripped like csvField. Name files scan_<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.csv. Append to _band.csv for tagged sources. Keep a [hex: (count, firstMs, lastMs, label, category, Set<address>)] tally and write _unique.csv in stopSession. Log before the 1.5 s dedupe, or drop the dedupe for logging. GPS needs CLLocationManager and NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription (absent from Info.plist); that part belongs with the Map area.

gaps.title: Local heard counter (RX) and visible scan status
gaps.androidBehaviour: packetsHeard is incremented for every Disney advert, including ones the show-control filter drops. TelemetryLine shows "MM/RF BLE:OFF|SCAN|LINK | RX:n | … | SCAN:ON | LOG:REC". Scan problems are published as status text ("Turn on Bluetooth", "scan failed (scanning too frequently)", "Scanning (screen off)").
gaps.iosState: The iPhone scan has no heard counter. telemetryLine's RX and the scan pill number come from androidRemote.packetsHeard only; the local scan contributes just "iSCAN:ON" / "BACKUP:REC". vm.statusMessage ("Turn on Bluetooth", "Allow Bluetooth in Settings", "Listening for Disney BLE…") is assigned but no live view renders it, so a dead scanner looks the same as a quiet room.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add @Published iscanPacketsHeard, incremented on the first line of handlePacket (before the filter, as Android does). Add "iRX:n" to telemetryLine, show it in scanStatusPills and as a HEARD row in ISCanView.statsBlock. Render statusMessage, or at least the Bluetooth off / unauthorised state, in TelemetryBar.

gaps.title: Android-remote scan panel: show-control toggle and source address not exposed over the relay
gaps.androidBehaviour: The Android Scan tab has the SHOW-CTRL / ALL RAW chip and per-row address / BAND. Neither reaches the relay protocol: RelayCommands.execute has no action for show_control_only, and LivePacketDto / livePacketsJson carry only hex, label, rssi, note, category, typeInfo, dedupeKey, timestampMs.
gaps.iosState: RemoteScanView (ANDROID SCAN / RX) offers Scan/Pause, Log, Clr, Vib, GROUPED/RAW, CLASS and Auto-response. It has no show-control toggle and no address / band on rows. AndroidRemotePacket has no address or isBand.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Android side: new action set_show_control_only {enabled} calling store.saveShowControlOnly, showControlOnly in statusJson, and address + isBand added to LivePacketDto / livePacketsJson. iOS side: parse showControlOnly into AndroidRemoteStatus, add the toggle and vm.setAndroidShowControlOnly to RemoteScanView.controlRow, add address / isBand to AndroidRemotePacket and the subtitle.

gaps.title: Persisted scan UI state (collapsed sections, scan on/off); resume clears the feed
gaps.androidBehaviour: Collapsed scan sections persist in SharedPreferences "magicmaker_ui" key scan_collapsed_sections (string set of LivePacketSection names). The scan on/off choice persists as scan_active and is restored on service start. Resuming a paused scan keeps the existing live buffers.
gaps.iosState: collapsedLocalSections / collapsedScanSections are in-memory @Published sets in RemoteUIState and are lost on relaunch. Local scanning is always forced on at launch (setLocalListening(true)), ignoring a previous Pause. setLocalListening(true) calls clearIscanLive(), so Pause then Scan wipes the feed.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Persist the two collapsed sets in UserDefaults (array of LivePacketSection.rawValue) in the toggle functions and load them in RemoteUIState.init. Persist a local scan_active Bool in setLocalListening and honour it in bootstrapAfterLaunch (default true). Remove the clearIscanLive() call from setLocalListening.

gaps.title: Wide / tablet layout (controls beside feed, two-column rows)
gaps.androidBehaviour: isWideLayout() (screenWidthDp >= 600) makes WideScreenColumns put controls in a 34% left column and the feed in 66%. RAW uses LazyVerticalGrid(2); GROUPED chunks rows in pairs.
gaps.iosState: Single-column stack on every size class, although the target includes iPad (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY 1,2).
gaps.whatIosNeeds: In RemoteScanTabView read @Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass); when .regular, lay out as HStack (controls about 34%, results about 66%) and use a two-column LazyVGrid or paired rows for the feed.

gaps.title: A heard wand colour updates the Wand display
gaps.androidBehaviour: In handleHeard, a heard packet classified as starlight sets UiState.wandDisplayColorIndex (starlightLearnColorIndex ?: starlightColorIndex), so the Wand tab mirrors the last wand colour heard.
gaps.iosState: vm.wandDisplayColorIndex changes only from the Android status poll or the phone's own transmit; a Starlight packet heard by the iPhone scan does not touch it.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: In appendLocalLivePacket, when classified?.typeInfo == "starlight", call applyWandDisplayColorIndex(MagicClassifier.starlightLearnColorIndex(hex) ?? MagicClassifier.starlightColorIndex(hex)).

gaps.title: Battery-optimisation banner ("Unrestricted battery required for screen-off scan" / OPT OUT)
gaps.androidBehaviour: ScanTab shows an amber banner with an OPT OUT button while BatteryOptimization.isIgnored(ctx) is false; it launches the ignore-battery-optimisation system intent.
gaps.iosState: None.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Android-only OS facility (Doze / battery-optimisation whitelist). iOS has no equivalent API.

gaps.title: RUN IN BACKGROUND switch, start on boot, foreground service keep-alive
gaps.androidBehaviour: A switch writes start_on_boot (prefs "magicmaker") for BootReceiver. Scanning lives in a START_STICKY foreground service with a partial wake lock and restarts itself in onTaskRemoved; the tab shows "Service running · lock screen OK".
gaps.iosState: None. The app declares the bluetooth-central background mode only.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Boot receiver, foreground service and wake lock are Android-only facilities that keep the phone alive as an unattended scanner / transmitter host.

gaps.title: Screen-off / background scanning (manufacturer-data ScanFilter, restart on screen change, scan-failure codes)
gaps.androidBehaviour: With the screen off the service restarts the scan with a ScanFilter on manufacturer id 0x0183 so results keep flowing; screen-on returns to an unfiltered scan. Both use SCAN_MODE_LOW_LATENCY. onScanFailed codes are mapped to text and the scan restarts after 800 ms.
gaps.iosState: The scan uses scanForPeripherals(withServices: nil, AllowDuplicates: true). BleCoordinator restarts it on background / foreground and reports "Listening (background OK)", which is misleading.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing for parity. Worth correcting the "Listening (background OK)" text and telling the user scanning needs the app in the foreground.
gaps.notApplicableReason: CoreBluetooth only delivers background scan results for explicit service UUIDs. Disney packets are manufacturer-data adverts with no service UUID, so an iPhone cannot hear them while backgrounded or locked.

gaps.title: Library file on shared storage (GRANT ACCESS, path, EXPORT / IMPORT) in the Scan controls
gaps.androidBehaviour: LibraryFileSection shows /sdcard/MagicMaker/magicmaker_library.json, requests all-files access, and offers EXPORT (store.exportLibrary) and IMPORT (store.importLibrary).
gaps.iosState: No control. Documents (magicmaker_store.json, iscan_backup/) is already visible in the Files app because UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace are set.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing for the permission and path. An in-app export / import (fileExporter / fileImporter) of the library JSON is a library-area decision and only matters once iOS keeps its own library.
gaps.notApplicableReason: All-files access and the /sdcard path are Android-only. iOS already exposes the app's Documents folder in Files without a permission flow.

gaps.title: Tap a row to broadcast it from the phone itself
gaps.androidBehaviour: onTap calls MagicMakerForegroundService.transmit(ctx, pkt.hex), which queues a local manufacturer-data advertise burst.
gaps.iosState: Tap calls vm.transmitAndroidHex(hex), which sends the relay "transmit" command. The row is disabled when no relay is linked.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing; the relay path is already in place. Only the row itself should be disabled without a relay, not its other actions, once those exist.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Needs BLE manufacturer-data advertising, which an iPhone cannot do. iOS already routes the tap through the Android / ESP32 relay.

gaps.title: Relay-host side of scanning (live feed JSON, remote scan / log / clear / remove handlers, relay-advert skipping)
gaps.androidBehaviour: The service answers iPhone commands: setScan, setRecording, clearLive, removeLive, removeRawLive, saveCustomPreset, liveJson (the last 120 raw packets), statusJson. BleScanner skips adverts that carry the relay service UUID and treats "MM:" local names as relay commands.
gaps.iosState: iOS is the client of all of these (setAndroidScan, setAndroidRecording, clearAndroidLive, removeAndroid*Live, saveAndroidCustomPreset, fetchLivePackets).
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing; iOS should not host a relay.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Exists only so Android can act as the transmitter / relay host for the iPhone.

logicDrift.what: Show-control filter predicate: Android MagicClassifier.isShowControl (TLV walk) vs iOS classify(hex) == nil (E?00E9 regex). An E9 record with no channel marker is invisible to iOS. This is the shape of Android's own built-in presets (PacketBuilder.preset / dual / rainbow5 / circle).
logicDrift.androidResult: Kept. Row "SINGLE COLOR: RED" in COLORS, dedupe key C1:15; lightsBand is true so it drives the strip.
logicDrift.iosResult: classify returns nil, so the packet is dropped entirely with the filter on (the default). With the filter off it is "RAW PACKET" in UNKNOWN, key RAW:<hex>.

logicDrift.what: Wake-ping-prefixed effects. Android classifies by the E9 record; iOS returns "ping" for anything starting 8301CC03 that is not one of its 11 showBlocks.
logicDrift.androidResult: "SINGLE COLOR: RED", typeInfo single, section COLORS, dedupe key C1:15 (its own GROUPED row).
logicDrift.iosResult: "INTERACTION PING", typeInfo ping, section PING, dedupe key FUNC:ping. Every ping-prefixed effect and every plain ping share one GROUPED row, overwritten by the latest.

logicDrift.what: showBlocks tables differ (Android has 2 entries, iOS has 11), so the same hex lands in a different section.
logicDrift.androidResult: "SINGLE COLOR: BLUE" in COLORS (not a show block on Android).
logicDrift.iosResult: "SHOW: AMBIENT BLUE", typeInfo show_block, in SHOWS.

logicDrift.what: Ping labels. Android uses DisneyTlv.pingName; iOS has two fixed strings.
logicDrift.androidResult: 8301CC03000000 is "Signal Beacon"; 8301CC03000100 is "Wake Ping".
logicDrift.iosResult: 8301CC03000000 is "Interaction Ping"; 8301CC03000100 is "Interaction Ping (Fast Mode)".

logicDrift.what: Beacon families (E4/E5/EA/EF) with the filter off. Android has classifyEffectFamily; iOS has no equivalent.
logicDrift.androidResult: With ALL RAW: "SYNC CUE (E501)", category ANIMATION, section ANIMATIONS. Dropped with SHOW-CTRL on.
logicDrift.iosResult: With the filter off: "RAW PACKET", section UNKNOWN. Dropped with the filter on (same as Android).

logicDrift.what: Row label for an unclassified packet in the live feed.
logicDrift.androidResult: "?" (handleHeard passes classified?.label ?: "?").
logicDrift.iosResult: "RAW PACKET".
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301C0021234 (filter off)

logicDrift.what: Radio-level dedupe. iOS BleCentral drops a repeat of the same key within 1.5 s before anything sees it; Android has none. Affects the RAW view, the log and any counter.
logicDrift.androidResult: 10 RAW rows and 10 log rows (buffer capped at 120).
logicDrift.iosResult: 1 RAW row and 1 log row.
logicDrift.exampleInput: The same advert (e.g. 8301E100E905002E0EF5B0) received 10 times in 1 second

logicDrift.what: Deleting a row in GROUPED view.
logicDrift.androidResult: removeLive(dedupeKey) removes that key from both livePackets and rawLivePackets; it is gone from RAW too.
logicDrift.iosResult: removeIscanUnique only touches iscanUniqueLive; the packets are still listed in RAW.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Delete "Single Color: Red" (key C1:15) in GROUPED, then switch to RAW

logicDrift.what: Live buffer size.
logicDrift.androidResult: 120 entries each for unique and raw (MAX_LIVE).
logicDrift.iosResult: 200 each (maxIscanLive).
logicDrift.exampleInput: 150 distinct packets heard

logicDrift.what: Subtitle of rows in the iOS Android-remote feed. iOS shows note if non-empty, else RSSI; Android always sends note "Heard".
logicDrift.androidResult: "RSSI -62 · AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF | HEARD".
logicDrift.iosResult: "HEARD"; RSSI is never shown for relay rows.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Any packet in the Android relay live list

logicDrift.what: Android-remote GROUPED list. Android keeps a separate unique list of 120; liveJson ships only the last 120 raw packets and iOS derives "unique" from those.
logicDrift.androidResult: GROUPED shows two rows: Single Color: Red and Wake Ping.
logicDrift.iosResult: Remote GROUPED shows only the ping; the colour has scrolled out of the raw window.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Android hears Single Color: Red once, then 120 wake pings

logicDrift.what: Pausing or resuming the Android scan from the iPhone vs from the Android UI. The relay setScan handler does not update userWantsScan, save prefs, or start/stop logging; ACTION_SET_SCAN does all three.
logicDrift.androidResult: Local PAUSE: userWantsScan=false, persisted, logging stopped, scan stays off.
logicDrift.iosResult: Relay set_scan(false): the scan stops, but userWantsScan stays true, so ensureScanning() restarts it after the next transmit or screen change and logging continues. Relay set_scan(true) after a local PAUSE does nothing, because startScanNow returns when !userWantsScan.
logicDrift.exampleInput: iPhone taps Pause on ANDROID SCAN, then taps any TX row

logicDrift.what: Auto-response fired from the scan path.
logicDrift.androidResult: Only for classified packets; sends the whole response sequence (sendSequence(responseHexes)); trigger matching sees custom presets and the learned library.
logicDrift.iosResult: Also fires for unclassified packets; sends only rule.responseHexes.first; matchesTriggerId is called with learned: [], so triggers that reference learned or custom packets cannot match.
logicDrift.exampleInput: A rule with 3 response packets triggered by a heard wake ping

summary:
Android has a full LOGS tab (session list, per-log filters, Analyze, add-to-library, delete, timed replay) built on a 13-column CSV plus two sidecar files. iOS has none of the viewer; its only live logger writes 3 columns, and the fuller session code in MagicStore.swift is dead (RecordTab/FilesTab are never mounted, and handlePacket returns before the store whenever local listening is on, which is always).

**Session file format — not compatible today**

| | Android | iOS live path | iOS dead path (MagicStore.swift) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Directory | `/sdcard/MagicMaker/logs` if all-files access; else `Android/data/<pkg>/files/scan_sessions`; else `filesDir/scan_sessions`. Reads all three. | `Documents/iscan_backup/` | `Documents/scan_sessions/` |
| File name | `scan_<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.csv`, local time, no zone | `iscan_<ISO8601 UTC, ':'→'-'>Z.csv` | `scan_<ISO8601 UTC>Z.csv` |
| Sidecars | `<base>_band.csv` (same header), `<base>_unique.csv` (`hex,count,first_ms,last_ms,label,category,addresses`) | none | none |
| Header | `timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note,source_address,is_band,lat,lng,accuracy` | `timestamp_ms,hex,rssi` | `timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note` |
| Escaping | commas/newlines in label, colors, note become spaces | n/a | none |

- **iOS live file read by Android:** `readLog` requires at least 6 columns, so every 3-column row is rejected and the log shows 0 packets.
- **iOS 8-column file read by Android:** parses, with empty address, band=false and no GPS; rows with a comma in `colors` (E913) shift columns.
- **Android file read by iOS:** no CSV reader exists on iOS.
- Columns 0–2 (epoch ms, canonical uppercase hex, RSSI) are identical everywhere, so adopting Android's header on iOS is a strict superset.

Android's LogsTab has no share or CSV-export button; logs are simply files on shared storage. The only EXPORT/IMPORT buttons are for the library JSON in LibraryFileSection.

On iOS: parse those in AndroidRemoteStatus.parse, add vm.replayAndroidLog/stopAndroidReplay, and show the banner and STOP in LogsTabView. notes:
Line numbers are for HEAD 4f78528 (v1.3.10). That commit landed while I was reading and shifted lines in ServiceState.kt and in MagicMakerForegroundService.kt after line 1075; all refs above are post-commit. Nothing was edited in the repo; one throwaway Java file was written under the session scratchpad to confirm the Gson behaviour below.

**iOS dead code.** RecordTab, FilesTab, PresetsTab, AutoTab, LabTab and RemoteMoreView compile but are never instantiated (ContentView.swift:98-108). That makes vm.toggleRecording, vm.livePackets and MagicStore.beginScanSession/endScanSession/appendToSession/persistRecording unreachable. Separately, handlePacket returns at AppViewModel.swift:189-196 whenever local listening is on, so store.processHeardPacket never runs in normal use either.

**Android defects found in this area (do not port verbatim):**
- **Library save fails without a GPS fix.** Recording.lat/lng are NaN when there is no location (MagicModels.kt:39-40; MagicMakerForegroundService.kt:1072-1073), and MagicStore uses a default GsonBuilder (MagicStore.kt:23). I confirmed with gson 2.10 (the app pins 2.10.1) that the default builder throws IllegalArgumentException on NaN. So while any no-fix recording sits in the 500-entry `recordings` list, save() fails silently (logged to CrashLog as "MagicStore.save", MagicStore.kt:280-300) and exportLibrary() returns null, which the UI reports as "Grant storage access first" (MagicMakerScreens.kt:590-595). Swift's JSONEncoder throws on NaN too, so iOS should use Double? for these fields.
- **isLibraryNoise hides real light effects.** It treats every 8301CC03 prefix as a ping (MagicClassifier.kt:356-362), so wake-prefixed effects such as the built-in "Lightning" (8301CC03000100E100E90C…, PresetCatalog.kt:27, 33) are hidden by default in ANALYZE and skipped by ADD ALL → LIB, even though classify and isShowControl treat them as effects. The correct test is "CC record with no E9 record", which is the same pings-versus-light-effects distinction the owner asked for in the scanner.
- **The LOG toggle is not sticky.** ensureLoggingStarted forces recordSession = true on every scan start (MagicMakerForegroundService.kt:599-600) and ACTION_SET_RECORDING never saves the pref (334-348). The effective Android behaviour is "always log while scanning; LOG pauses until the next scan start".

**Overlap with other areas.** The band-tagging UI (BandConfigSection), the MAP tab (which is built entirely from the lat/lng/address columns), PacketSync and the classifier differences are only covered here as far as they change log contents.

summary: iOS has none of this area: no CoreLocation, no MapKit, no location usage string, no map tab, and its scan callback discards the advertiser identity. Android keeps the latest GPS/network fix in the foreground service, stamps every logged packet with lat/lng/accuracy and source MAC in a 13-column session CSV, and the MAP tab re-reads those CSVs to plot capture points (bucketed to about 1.1 m cells) and RSSI-weighted transmitter estimates on OpenStreetMap tiles. There are five real gaps (roughly 450-500 lines of Swift plus one Info.plist key, no third-party dependency), three not-applicable items and five logic drifts. Separately, Android's NaN "no fix" sentinel makes its own library save throw (confirmed against Gson 2.10; details in notes). Nothing was built or run on a device.

gaps.title: Location capture while scanning (latest fix held in memory)
gaps.androidBehaviour: MagicMakerForegroundService.startLocationUpdates() runs at the end of boot(). If ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted it seeds `lastLocation` from getLastKnownLocation(GPS_PROVIDER) ?: getLastKnownLocation(NETWORK_PROVIDER), then requests updates from both providers every 2000 ms / 0 m. The LocationListener only overwrites the @Volatile `lastLocation`. stopLocationUpdates() is called from shutdown(). There is no age or accuracy check: the last fix from either provider is used however old it is. ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is part of corePerms requested at first launch, and the whole UI is gated behind it ("PERMS REQUIRED: BT · LOC · NOTIFY").
gaps.iosState: Absent. A search of ios/ for CoreLocation, CLLocation, MapKit, latitude, longitude and NSLocation returns no hits. Info.plist carries only Bluetooth, camera and local-network usage strings.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: New class, e.g. ios/MagicMaker/BLE/LocationTagger.swift (about 50 lines): NSObject + CLLocationManagerDelegate owning a CLLocationManager (desiredAccuracy = kCLLocationAccuracyBest, distanceFilter = kCLDistanceFilterNone) with `private(set) var last: CLLocation?`. start() calls requestWhenInUseAuthorization() when status is .notDetermined, then startUpdatingLocation(); locationManagerDidChangeAuthorization starts updates once authorized; didUpdateLocations sets last = locations.last; stop() calls stopUpdatingLocation(). gaps.title: Every logged packet stamped with lat/lng/accuracy and source address (13-column session CSV)

Header: `timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note,source_address,is_band,lat,lng,accuracy`. lat/lng/accuracy are written as empty strings when missing; commas and newlines in label/colors/note are replaced with spaces (csvField). The address is the advertiser MAC from ScanResult.device.address. Logging is always on while scanning (ensureLoggingStarted() at boot and on ACTION_SET_SCAN), so every scan produces a geotagged log.

gaps.title: Map data loader: stream GPS-tagged rows from all logs and bucket them into capture points
gaps.androidBehaviour: MagicStore.forEachLoggedLocation() streams every chronological scan CSV in all log dirs (skipping *_band.csv and *_unique.csv), drops the header, splits each line on ",", ignores rows with fewer than 12 fields or an unparseable c[10]/c[11], and yields lat=c[10], lng=c[11], rssi=c[2] (0 if unparseable), address=c[8], label=c[3], category=c[4]. The accuracy column is not read. loadMapData() rejects NaN, (0,0) and out-of-range coordinates, buckets by round(lat*1e5),round(lng*1e5) (about 1.1 m cells), keeps the first row's lat/lng/label (blank becomes "Capture")/category per bucket plus a count, sorts by count descending and keeps the top 1000 (MAX_MARKERS). It runs on Dispatchers.IO and re-runs whenever storeRevision changes. readLog() also parses lat/lng/accuracy into LoggedPacket, but no screen displays them; the map is the only consumer of location.
gaps.iosState: iOS has no CSV reader of any kind (no equivalent of readLog, listLogs or forEachLoggedLocation). MagicStore.refreshSessions() and ISCanBackupLogger.listSessions() only list file URLs.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: New pure-Swift file, e.g. ios/MagicMaker/Core/CaptureMapData.swift: structs CapturePoint{lat,lng,count,label,category}, TxEstimate{address,lat,lng,count,bestRssi,radiusM,label}, MapData{captures,transmitters}, and a loader that enumerates Documents/iscan_backup/*.csv and Documents/scan_sessions/*.csv and reads them line by line off the main actor. Split with components(separatedBy: ","), not split(separator:), which drops empty fields and shifts the column indices. Require count >= 12, Double(c[10]) and Double(c[11]); apply the same validity checks, 1e-5 bucketing, sort and 1000 cap. Existing 3-column and 8-column iOS files are skipped by the count >= 12 rule. No new storage is needed: Android keeps no location table or cache, the session CSVs are the only source.

gaps.title: Estimated transmitter positions (RSSI-weighted centroid per source address)
gaps.androidBehaviour: For every valid row with a non-blank address, TxAccum.add() accumulates weight w = max(rssi + 100, 1)^2, the sums of w*lat, w*lng, w*lat^2, w*lng^2, the observation count, the best RSSI and the label of the best-RSSI row (label, or category when the label is blank). estimate() returns centroid = sum(w*lat)/sum(w), sum(w*lng)/sum(w) and radius = sqrt(varLat*111320^2 + varLng*(111320*cos(lat))^2) clamped to 5..500 m. Only addresses with at least 3 observations (MIN_TX_OBSERVATIONS) are kept, sorted by count descending, top 1000.
gaps.iosState: Absent, and not computable today because no source identifier is logged.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Port TxAccum and the filter/sort/cap verbatim into the loader file (about 45 lines of arithmetic), keyed by the logged source id (CBPeripheral.identifier UUID string). It depends on the source-id column from the stamping gap, and on logging each advert per source (see the dedupe drift), otherwise the n >= 3 threshold is rarely reached.

logicDrift.what: Session CSV schema. The Android map loader requires at least 12 columns with lat at index 10 and lng at index 11; neither iOS log format has them.
logicDrift.exampleInput: One heard ping 8301CC03000100 at RSSI -60
logicDrift.androidResult: 13 fields: <ts>,8301CC03000100,-60,<label>,SHOW,ping,,Ping (not saved),<MAC>,false,<lat>,<lng>,<accuracy>
logicDrift.iosResult: Default path (ISCanBackupLogger): 3 fields `<ts>,8301CC03000100,-60`. Record path (MagicStore): 8 fields ending at note. Fed to Android's forEachLoggedLocation, both are skipped (c.size < 12), giving zero map points.

logicDrift.what: CSV field escaping. Android replaces commas and newlines in label/colors/note with spaces; the iOS session writer emits them raw, so a comma inside a field shifts every later column.
logicDrift.exampleInput: An E913 "Corner Alternate" packet, whose colors string on both platforms is "<A> centre, <B> / <C>"
logicDrift.androidResult: colors written as "<A> centre  <B> / <C>"; the row keeps 13 fields and lat/lng stay at indices 10/11
logicDrift.iosResult: colors written with the comma; the row has 9 fields instead of 8. If lat/lng were appended without scrubbing they would land one index late and the row would be skipped or misread.

logicDrift.what: De-duplication before logging. Android forwards and logs every scan result; iOS suppresses repeats of the same key for 1.5 s, and the key has no source in it. Observation counts, the n >= 3 transmitter threshold and the RSSI weighting all differ.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Two beacons each repeat the same hex 10 times per second for 3 s while the phone stands still
logicDrift.androidResult: About 60 rows; the capture point shows "×60"; each MAC has n = 30, so two transmitter estimates are produced
logicDrift.iosResult: 2 callbacks in total (t = 0 and t = 1.5 s), with the two sources indistinguishable; count would be ×2 and no source would reach n >= 3

logicDrift.what: Source identity. Android records the advertiser MAC; iOS drops the peripheral entirely, and the only identity CoreBluetooth offers is a per-iPhone UUID.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Any Disney advert from a fixed park beacon
logicDrift.androidResult: source_address = "7C:9E:BD:12:34:56" (stable for fixed beacons; rotating for private addresses)
logicDrift.iosResult: No source today. After the port it would be CBPeripheral.identifier, e.g. "E621E1F8-C36C-495A-93FC-0C247A3E6E5F", which never matches an Android MAC or another iPhone's id, so transmitter groups cannot be merged across devices.

logicDrift.what: Session file name time base. Android uses local time without a zone; iOS uses UTC ISO-8601 with a trailing Z. Minor, but name-sorted lists mix time bases if files from both are combined.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Session started 2026-11-14 09:30:05 local time, UTC-5
logicDrift.iosResult: scan_2026-11-14T14-30-05Z.csv (and iscan_2026-11-14T14-30-05Z.csv for the backup log)

summary: iOS has no diagnostics surface for its own scanner: no DIAG tab, no per-source stats, no crash log, no local RX or auto-reply counters, and its own status string is written but never drawn. The most user-visible gap is the Scan strip: Android v1.3.10 made it follow only packets that light the band, while the iOS strip still shows any packet (pings, beacons, wand colours) and ignores the iPhone's own scan entirely. iOS mirrors Android's telemetry over the relay well, but that is Android's data, not the iPhone's. Nothing was compiled or run (no Swift toolchain here); all findings are from reading both sides in full.

gaps.title: Scan strip follows only packets that light the band (lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard)
gaps.androidBehaviour: handleHeard computes lights = BandEffectModel.from(hex).lightsBand (kind is not NONE, PING or WAND) and updates UiState.lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard on every packet, including inside the 250 ms UI throttle. ScanTab draws LastHeardStrip(state.lastLightHex, state.lightsHeard), titled 'LAST LIGHTS · #n' or 'LAST LIGHTS · NONE HEARD YET'. statusJson exports all three fields to the relay.

LastHeardStrip takes the newest of vm.livePackets and vm.androidLivePackets with no light filter, so relay pings, beacons and wand colours replace the last effect. vm.livePackets is only filled when isRecording && !isLocalListening; isLocalListening is forced true at launch and RecordTab is not mounted, so the iPhone's own scan (iscanRawLive / iscanUniqueLive) never reaches the strip. The title 'LAST HEARD · n LIVE' is a buffer size, not a lights count. Swift BandEffectModel has no lightsBand, and AndroidRemoteStatus.parse drops lastLightHex / lastLightLabel / lightsHeard.

Android does not reset these on clear. 3) AndroidRemoteStatus: add lastLightHex, lastLightLabel, lightsHeard and parse the JSON keys of the same names. 4) LastHeardStrip: stop reading vm.livePackets; show the local lastLightHex when the iPhone scanner has one, else androidRemote.lastLightHex; title 'LAST LIGHTS · #n'; empty text 'LAST LIGHTS · NONE HEARD YET'. gaps.title: RX and TX-AUTO counters for the iPhone's own scanner

gaps.title: Own Bluetooth state and status string visible to the user
gaps.androidBehaviour: TelemetryLine's second token is the radio state: BLE:OFF (not running), BLE:SCAN or BLE:LINK. UiState.status carries every engine message: scan-failure reasons, 'Scan error: …', 'Turn on Bluetooth', 'Scanning (screen off)', advertiser and relay errors, 'Auto→label (n)'. It is drawn as 'STATUS: …' in the Relay panel and in the ongoing notification. A top banner 'PERMS REQUIRED: BT · LOC · NOTIFY' with a GRANT button appears while permissions are missing.
gaps.iosState: AppViewModel.statusMessage is assigned in about 50 places but no view reads it; the only references in Views are two writes. So 'Turn on Bluetooth', 'Allow Bluetooth in Settings', 'Catalog sync timed out…' and 'Android TX failed' never reach the screen. The second telemetry token is the relay backend name ('BLE' or 'WIFI'), not the radio state. With Bluetooth off or denied the user sees only the amber relay hint 'Open LINK — tap Retry BLE…'. The LINK tab does show Android's status string, but not the iPhone's own.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: 1) Draw vm.statusMessage: a 'STATUS' remoteRow in RemoteLinkView and ISCanView.statsBlock, or a third line in TelemetryBar. 2) Publish the radio state as data, not only a string: BleCentral.centralManagerDidUpdateState forwards CBManagerState through a new delegate method to AppViewModel @Published bleState. telemetryLine then emits 'iBLE:OFF', 'iBLE:DENIED', 'iBLE:SCAN' or 'iBLE:IDLE'. 3) An amber banner in ContentView when the state is .unauthorized or .poweredOff, with a button opening UIApplication.openSettingsURLString; this is the equivalent of Android's PERMS REQUIRED row, and Bluetooth is the only permission involved on iOS.

gaps.title: Scan-failure error-code status and screen-off scan mode status
gaps.androidBehaviour: ScanCallback.onScanFailed(code) leads to restartScanDelayed, which maps codes 1-6 to status text ('scan failed (scanning too frequently)' and so on) and restarts the scan after 800 ms. startScanNow reports 'Scan error: …'. These are status strings only; Android keeps no numeric restart or error counter.
gaps.iosState: CoreBluetooth has no scan-failed callback or start quota. The nearest equivalent, CBManagerState changes, is produced as a string but never drawn. iOS restarts its scan on background and foreground transitions.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing beyond the status-string gap.

logicDrift.what: What the Scan strip shows for the same heard sequence
logicDrift.exampleInput: Heard in order: 8301CC03000100E100E90500090E02B0 (single-colour effect), then 8301CC03000100 (wake ping)
logicDrift.androidResult: The strip keeps animating the blue effect, titled 'LAST LIGHTS · #1'. The ping has kind PING, lightsBand is false, and lastLightHex is unchanged.
logicDrift.iosResult: The strip switches to the ping: BandEffectModel kind .ping, all five LEDs dim, titled 'LAST HEARD · 2 LIVE'. That happens only when both packets arrive through the Android relay feed; the same two packets heard by the iPhone's own scanner never reach the strip at all.

logicDrift.what: Show-control filter predicate. Android uses MagicClassifier.isShowControl (a TLV walk for an E9 record); iOS uses classify(hex) != nil (a regex for E?00E9 that is not byte-aligned). Everything downstream (live feed, CSV, auto-reply, any future source stats) inherits the difference.
logicDrift.exampleInput: (a) 8301E90500090E02B0, an E9 record with no channel marker. (b) 8301C0041E100E95, band telemetry whose payload nibbles happen to spell E100E9.
logicDrift.androidResult: (a) Kept: the TLV chain has an E9 record, classified 'Single Color: Blue'. (b) Dropped: the only record is C0, classify returns null and isShowControl is false; only packetsHeard is incremented.
logicDrift.iosResult: (a) Dropped: there is no E?00E9 prelude, so classify returns nil; it is never shown, logged or counted. (b) Kept: the regex matches across byte boundaries and it is classified 'Show Control: E95', category animation, section CONTROL.

logicDrift.what: Classification of a wake-ping-prefixed effect and of the bare wake ping. iOS checks the showBlocks table and the 8301CC03 prefix before looking for an E9 record; Android walks the TLV chain. This changes the label, category and section that any diagnostics category set would report.
logicDrift.androidResult: (a) 'Wake Ping', typeInfo ping, section INTERROGATE, dedupe key FUNC:ping. (b) 'Single Color: Blue', typeInfo single, category COLOR, section COLORS.
logicDrift.iosResult: (a) 'Show: Wakeup Ping', typeInfo show_block, section SHOWS, dedupe key SHOW:8301CC03000100. (b) 'Show: Ambient Blue', typeInfo show_block, category SHOW, section SHOWS.

logicDrift.what: Duplicate handling before counting. Android has no scanner-level dedupe; iOS drops repeats of the same key for 1.5 s inside BleCentral, before the view model, the backup CSV or any counter sees them.
logicDrift.exampleInput: One wand broadcasting the same Starlight colour 10 times a second for 3 s (30 adverts)
logicDrift.androidResult: packetsHeard +30, rawLivePackets +30 (capped at 120), SourceStat.count 30, 30 session-log rows.
logicDrift.iosResult: 2 deliveries (at t=0 and t≥1.5 s): iscanRawLive +2 and 2 CSV lines. Any RX or per-source counter added downstream of BleCentral would read 2.

logicDrift.what: Odd-length hex. Android's HexUtils.hexToBytes drops the trailing nibble and DisneyTlv.parse returns null; iOS's HexUtils.hexToBytes has precondition(clean.count % 2 == 0), which traps. The Lab hex TextField reaches it on every keystroke through BandPreviewView → BandEffectModel.from, LabBuilderPanel.summaryCard and legacyAdvertiseRejectReason. Found by reading only; not run.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Lab hex field containing 8301CC0300010 (the default wake ping with one character deleted)
logicDrift.androidResult: The preview shows 'No packet' and the app keeps running. The code comment says callers run on every keystroke and must not crash.
logicDrift.iosResult: Precondition failure, so the app terminates; with no crash log, nothing records it.

logicDrift.what: Telemetry line composition for the same Android state
logicDrift.exampleInput: Android state: running, scanActive, packetsHeard=42, autoResponsesSent=0, autoEnabled
logicDrift.androidResult: 'MM/RF BLE:SCAN | RX:42 | TX-AUTO:0 | SCAN:ON | AUTO:ARM'. The second token is the radio state and TX-AUTO is always shown.
logicDrift.iosResult: 'MM/RF | BLE | RX:42 | SCAN:ON | AUTO:ARM | LIB:n | iSCAN:ON | BACKUP:REC'. The second token is the relay backend name, and TX-AUTO is hidden when 0.

logicDrift.what: Live buffer cap and the label of an unclassified packet
logicDrift.exampleInput: 150 distinct packets heard in ALL RAW mode, one of them 8301C00412345678
logicDrift.androidResult: The BUF figure tops out at 120 (MAX_LIVE); the unclassified row is labelled '?'.
logicDrift.iosResult: The BUF figure reaches 150 (cap 200, maxIscanLive); the unclassified row is labelled 'Raw packet'.

notes:
Facts that correct the brief's assumptions:
- Android keeps no numeric scan-restart or error counter. Failures surface only as UiState.status strings and CrashLog entries.
- The Android crash log is view-and-clear only; there is no export or share (MagicMakerScreens.kt:629-655).
- UiState.lastTransmitHex is declared and exported (ServiceState.kt:57, 308) but never assigned, so it is always "". It is not a gap.
- randomShow*, replay*, cloudSyncStatus, seenAddresses and sources are not in statusJson, and no relay command exposes sources or the crash log (RelayCommands.kt:162-163). iOS therefore cannot mirror those from Android.

Remaining UiState fields: storeRevision and labLoadTick are internal; wandDisplayColorIndex and the timing fields (wakeupPreambleMs, commandBurstMs, starlightBurstMs) belong to the wand and TX areas and are already mirrored.

Implementation cautions:
- The iOS dedupe at BleCentral.swift:190-201 sits upstream of everything. Any counter or source tally must be taken before it, or the dedupe must move into the view model.
- CoreBluetooth gives a per-app peripheral UUID, not a MAC. Sources are still feasible but should be labelled ID.
- iOS scans with withServices: nil (BleCentral.swift:82-85). Apple's background rules do not deliver such scans while backgrounded, so local counters will stall with the screen locked. BleCoordinator's 'Listening (background OK)' status (BleCoordinator.swift:140-144) is optimistic.
- statusJson is roughly 715-890 bytes with typical values (computed from the key list); v1.3.10 added about 127 bytes. RelayGattServer caches only the first 512 bytes on the characteristic (RelayGattServer.kt:175) but answers read-blob requests from the full buffer (98-111). The iOS side documents a 512-byte STATUS limit (AndroidRemoteClient.swift:437). I could not check whether iOS receives the whole status JSON over BLE; verify on a device before relying on the new lastLight* keys there. Wi-Fi /status is unaffected.

lightsBand counts Kind.COMPLEX even when no colours were decoded (undecoded E90C), so the Android strip will animate a red / yellow-orange placeholder for those.

Views/RecordTab.swift, FilesTab.swift, PresetsTab.swift, AutoTab.swift, LabTab.swift and RemoteMoreView are compiled but not mounted from ContentView.swift:98-108; LastHeardStrip's dependence on vm.livePackets is a leftover from that path.

summary: Android has a dedicated SETTINGS tab plus roughly 30 persisted preferences; iOS has no Settings screen and only 10 persisted keys. Of Android's transmission settings, iOS remote-controls three (wake, command burst, starlight burst) with narrower slider ranges and a wrong 2000 ms fallback, and has nothing for TX mode (interleave) or broadcast strength, because no relay command exists for either. Everything iOS "sets" lives on the Android phone, so with the ESP32 backend the timing sliders and both loops are silent no-ops: the firmware ACKs every command with {"ok":true} and ignores it, and wand colours go out for 4000 ms instead of 500 ms. iOS has nothing at all for the random light show and its interval, My MagicBand address tagging, settings backup in the library JSON, or cloud packet sync. Collapse state, scan/auto run-state and the Lab scratch packet are not persisted on iOS. At parity: lab_extended, the wand quick button, New Wand names, keep-awake, a local show-control-only toggle, and default-on logging. Five Android items are not applicable (OTA APK update, start-on-boot, battery exemption, relay host mode, all-files access). I found eight logic drifts; the one that bears directly on the owner's request is that the iOS scan strip has no lights-only filter and never shows the iPhone's own scan.

gaps.title: ESP32 backend: timing settings are silent no-ops (iOS has no local timing prefs)
gaps.androidBehaviour: Timings are local prefs read on every transmit: MagicTransmitter is built with lambdas over store.getWakeupPreambleMs / getCommandBurstMs / getStarlightBurstMs / getTxInterleave. Wand packets burst for starlight_burst_ms (default 500), standalone pings for 2000 ms, band commands wake then command.
gaps.iosState: Remote-control only. The sliders call set_wakeup_preamble / set_command_burst / set_starlight_burst; nothing is stored on the iPhone. With relayBackend == .esp32 the firmware replies {"ok":true} to every command and ignores these, so iOS reports 'Preamble 520ms' as success. The status read returns {"ok":true}, which parses to defaults, so the sliders snap back. Every command-path transmit uses DEFAULT_CMD_MS = 4000, including wand colours and pings, and WAKE_MS is fixed at 520.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Local persisted copies in UserDefaults (Int): command_burst_ms (default 4000, 500-12000), starlight_burst_ms (default 500, 250-5000), wakeup_preamble_ms (default 520). When backend == .esp32, route AppViewModel.transmitAndroidHex through the TX characteristic, which the firmware honours for 300-12000 ms: BleCentral.transmitViaRelayGatt(hex:durationMs:) writes "{hex}|{durationMs}". Use duration = starlightBurstMs for starlight, 2000 for a ping, commandBurstMs otherwise. Show WAKE as fixed 520 on ESP32 unless the firmware gains a command. Do not report success for set_* on ESP32. Seed the sliders from the local values when the status carries no timing keys.

gaps.title: TX loop and Wand loop: remote-only, no local engine or persistence
gaps.androidBehaviour: Prefs tx_loop_enabled (false), tx_loop_packet_id (Long, -1), tx_loop_interval_ms (Long, 3000, coerced 500-60000), and starlight_loop_enabled / starlight_loop_packet_id / starlight_interval_ms with the same shape. TxLoopSettingsSection has a LOOP switch and a 0.5-30 s slider; the Wand tab has the same. Loops run in the service, restart on boot, and are mutually exclusive with each other, the random show and keep-awake. A manual tap pre-empts and the loop resumes.
gaps.iosState: The toggles and 0.5-30 s sliders only forward set_tx_loop / set_starlight_loop and bind to androidRemote.txLoopEnabled / starlightLoopEnabled. Intervals live in RemoteUIState.txIntervalSec / wandIntervalSec, in memory. On ESP32 the command is ACKed and ignored: the status message says 'TX loop ON' but the toggle flips back and nothing repeats.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: A local loop scheduler in AppViewModel (Timer or Task) that sends the selected hex through the relay, waits for the interval after completion and repeats; only one loop active at a time. Use it when backend == .esp32, or always. Persist UserDefaults tx_loop_interval_ms (Int), tx_loop_packet_hex (String), starlight_interval_ms (Int), starlight_loop_packet_hex (String). Bind the toggles to local state when the relay has no loop support.

gaps.title: TX MODE (sustained / interleave) cannot be seen or changed from iOS; iOS has no Settings tab
gaps.androidBehaviour: A dedicated SETTINGS tab (SettingsTabScreen -> TransmissionSettingsSection) has a Switch 'TX MODE: INTERLEAVE / SUSTAINED' writing pref tx_interleave (Bool, default false). MagicTransmitter.sendBandCommand then chooses sendInterleaved (cycles = total / (slice*2), alternating a wake slice and a command slice) or sendSustained (wake for WAKE ms, then command for COMMAND ms). The slider captions change with the mode.
gaps.iosState: Nothing. MainTab is tx, wand, auto, lab, scan, link, with no settings case. There is no VM method and no relay action (RelayCommands.execute has no case), and the value is absent from statusJson and the catalog.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Android relay: add a RelayCommands action set_tx_interleave {enabled: Bool} with a Handlers field and a handler calling store.saveTxInterleave, and add txInterleave to ServiceState.statusJson. iOS: AndroidRemoteStatus.txInterleave, AppViewModel.setAndroidTxInterleave(_:), a new MainTab.settings case and a RemoteSettingsView holding the Toggle with Android's two explanatory strings, and move the three timing sliders there. Disable the toggle on ESP32, whose firmware is sustained-only.

gaps.title: BROADCAST STRENGTH (tx_power_level) missing
gaps.androidBehaviour: Four buttons MIN / LOW / MED / MAX write pref tx_power_level (Int 0..3, default 3). BleAdvertiser reads it through the txPowerLevel lambda and passes it to AdvertiseSettings.setTxPowerLevel (ULTRA_LOW..HIGH). The caption reads 'Lower = shorter range, fewer nearby bands react'.
gaps.iosState: Nothing: no UI, no relay action, not in status.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Android relay action set_tx_power {level: 0..3} calling store.saveTxPowerLevel, plus txPowerLevel in statusJson. iOS: AndroidRemoteStatus.txPowerLevel, AppViewModel.setAndroidTxPower(_:), and a 4-segment Picker in the settings view. ESP32 is fixed at ESP_PWR_LVL_P9 (firmware line 374), so show it as MAX and read-only.

gaps.title: Random light show and its interval setting
gaps.androidBehaviour: Lab -> RANDOM LIGHT SHOW has an INTERVAL SettingSlider (500-30000 ms, step 250), START SHOW / STOP SHOW, and the current packet label. Prefs are random_show_enabled (false) and random_show_interval_ms (Long, 3000, coerced 500-60000). The service picks LabPacketBuilder.buildRandomShow() on each burst (weighted preset / dual / crossfade / rainbow / circle / park effect, buzz about 1 in 5). The interval is live-adjustable, the show restarts on boot and resumes after a manual send.
gaps.iosState: Nothing. The iOS LabPacketBuilder has no buildRandomShow, there is no relay action for it, and it is not in the status.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Port buildRandomShow with showPaletteIds and randomShowEffects into ios/MagicMaker/Core/LabPacketBuilder.swift; the per-type builders already exist there. Add a section in RemoteLabView with the interval slider (500-30000 step 250), START/STOP and the label. Drive it with the local loop scheduler, sending 'transmit' through whichever relay is linked (this also works on ESP32). Persist random_show_interval_ms (Int, default 3000).

gaps.title: My MagicBand: band address tagging (band_addresses)
gaps.androidBehaviour: BandConfigSection on the Scan tab lists tagged addresses with REMOVE, a manual 'AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF' field with ADD, 'HEARD (TAP TO TAG)' showing the top 8 seenAddresses with rssi and count, and 'SAVED BAND PACKETS: n' with a confirmed DELETE ALL. Pref band_addresses is a comma-joined string of uppercase MACs (default empty); band_menu_collapsed (ui, true). Effects: isBand on live rows (highlight and '· BAND'), the tagged band's telemetry is whitelisted into the library, a scan_<stamp>_band.csv sidecar and an is_band CSV column are written, and Logs gets a BAND ONLY filter and replay.
gaps.iosState: Nothing. BleCentralDelegate delivers only (hex, rssi), IScanLivePacket has no address or isBand, and the relay live DTO (LivePacketDto) carries no address or isBand either.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: CoreBluetooth never exposes the advertiser MAC, so use peripheral.identifier.uuidString as the source id; manual MAC entry is not meaningful on iOS. Extend bleCentral(didReceive:rssi:) with source: String, add address and isBand to IScanLivePacket, keep a seen-sources list in AppViewModel (address, rssi, lastSeenMs, count; cap 80), store UserDefaults band_addresses ([String]), and add a collapsible section in ISCanView controls for tag / untag / remove. To tag Android-heard packets remotely, add address and isBand to LivePacketDto and relay actions add_band_address / remove_band_address.

gaps.title: Timing sliders: narrower ranges, different steps and defaults, no -/+ step buttons
gaps.androidBehaviour: WAKE SLICE 100-3000 ms step 50 (default 520, key wakeup_preamble_ms); COMMAND BURST 500-12000 ms step 50 (default 4000, key command_burst_ms); STARLIGHT WAND 250-5000 ms in 250 ms stops (default 500, key starlight_burst_ms). SettingSlider commits on release and has -/+ buttons for single-step nudges. Values are clamped again in MagicStore and MagicTransmitter.
gaps.iosState: Remote-only sliders inside a Lab DisclosureGroup: WAKE PREAMBLE 200...1500 step 20, COMMAND BURST 500...5000 step 100, STARLIGHT WAND 250...5000 step 100. Fallback defaults are 520 / 2000 / 500. There are no -/+ buttons and no mode-dependent captions.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Use the Android ranges and steps (100...3000/50, 500...12000/50, 250...5000/250) and a 4000 default for commandBurstMs in RemoteUIState, AndroidRemoteStatus, AndroidRemoteCatalog and the chunk-sync begin parse. Add -/+ buttons to sliderRow and rename the first slider WAKE SLICE with Android's captions. On Android, call publishTimingState() or bump storeRevision when the local Settings tab saves a timing, and fix the 2000 fallbacks at RelayCommands.kt:102 and CatalogSync.kt:25.

gaps.title: Android's show-control scan filter cannot be toggled from iOS
gaps.androidBehaviour: A Scan tab chip 'SHOW-CTRL' / 'ALL RAW' writes pref show_control_only (Bool, default true). When on, the service drops every packet failing MagicClassifier.isShowControl before the live feed, CSV log and library; that live feed is what the relay serves to iOS.

logicDrift.what: Scan strip: Android follows only packets that light the band; iOS shows the newest packet of any kind, and only from the Android relay. This is outside the settings area but is the parity item behind the owner's request.
logicDrift.exampleInput: An effect packet followed by the wake ping 8301CC03000100
logicDrift.androidResult: lastLightHex is updated only when BandEffectModel.from(hex).lightsBand (kind is not NONE, PING or WAND). The strip keeps animating the effect, titled 'LAST LIGHTS · #n'.
logicDrift.iosResult: LastHeardStrip takes the max timestamp of vm.livePackets and vm.androidLivePackets with no lights filter, so it switches to the ping and all LEDs go dim. vm.livePackets is only filled while isRecording, which is toggled only from the unreferenced RecordTab, so the iPhone's own scan (iscanRawLive) never reaches the strip. The iOS BandEffectModel has no lightsBand.

logicDrift.what: Show-control-only filter predicate. Android uses isShowControl (a TLV walk: any E9 record, a CC03 ping, CF9B/CF0B, or a show block). iOS uses classify(hex) != nil, and its classify needs the substring regex E[0-9A-F]00E9, i.e. a channel marker before E9.
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301E905002E0EFBB0 — the bare E905 white preset that PacketBuilder.preset emits on both platforms and the ESP32 relays unchanged
logicDrift.androidResult: Passes the filter and is shown as 'Single Color: White'.
logicDrift.iosResult: classify returns nil (no E?00E9 substring), so with the filter on (the default) the packet is dropped before the live list, backup log and iScan auto-response. The same applies to every marker-less builder packet (E906, E909, E90B).

logicDrift.what: A wake-ping-prefixed effect is labelled a ping on iOS. This feeds the iOS strip label and the section grouping.
logicDrift.androidResult: The TLV walk finds the E9 record: 'Single Color: Red', typeInfo single, category COLOR.
logicDrift.iosResult: The hasPrefix("8301CC03") check runs before the E9 parse: 'Interaction Ping', typeInfo ping, category SHOW. Only the handful of hexes listed in the iOS showBlocks escape this.

logicDrift.what: Command-burst default and fallback.
logicDrift.exampleInput: A status or catalog JSON without commandBurstMs, e.g. the ESP32 status {"ok":true}, or a fresh install
logicDrift.androidResult: 4000 ms (TransmitTiming.COMMAND_BURST_MS, UiState default). The ESP32 firmware's DEFAULT_CMD_MS is also 4000.
logicDrift.iosResult: The slider shows 2000 MS (AndroidRemoteStatus, AndroidRemoteCatalog and RemoteUIState defaults). Android's own relay fallbacks are also stale at 2000 (RelayCommands.kt:102, CatalogSync.kt:25).

logicDrift.what: Timing slider ranges.
logicDrift.exampleInput: COMMAND BURST set to 8000 ms on Android, or WAKE set to 100 or 3000 ms
logicDrift.androidResult: Valid: command 500-12000 and wake 100-3000 are stored and used.
logicDrift.iosResult: The iOS sliders are 500...5000 and 200...1500. The label prints the raw value ('8000MS') with the thumb pinned at max, and the next drag commits at most 5000 (or 1500), overwriting the Android value. The upper halves of Android's ranges are unreachable from iOS.

logicDrift.what: A timing changed in Android's own Settings tab is not reflected on iOS. The save neither updates ServiceState nor bumps storeRevision; publishTimingState is called only from the relay handlers.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Move WAKE SLICE from 520 to 800 on the Android Settings tab while the iPhone is linked

logicDrift.iosResult: The slider keeps showing 520, because the status is stale and the catalog is only re-pulled when storeRevision changes. Releasing the slider on iOS writes 520 back.

logicDrift.what: On-air time for a wand colour or ping sent from iOS depends on the relay, because iOS sends no duration on the command path.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Tap a Starlight colour on the iOS WAND tab
logicDrift.androidResult: Through the Android relay, or locally on Android, the burst lasts starlight_burst_ms (default 500 ms); a standalone ping lasts 2000 ms.
logicDrift.iosResult: Through the ESP32, the action 'transmit' is queued with DEFAULT_CMD_MS, so the wand colour or ping stays on air for 4000 ms.

logicDrift.what: Pausing the Android scanner locally versus from iOS. The relay handler does not touch userWantsScan or savePrefs.
logicDrift.exampleInput: {"action":"set_scan","enabled":false} from iOS, then any transmit
logicDrift.androidResult: The local SCAN / PAUSE button sets userWantsScan=false, saves scan_active and stops logging; the scan stays off across transmits and restarts.
logicDrift.iosResult: The remote pause only calls pauseScan(). ensureScanning() restarts the scan after the next TX because userWantsScan is still true, and nothing is persisted. area: CORE packet logic drift (classifier, TLV, patterns, hex utils, models, catalogs, builders, band effect model)
summary:
The iOS core is a port of an older Android classifier. Android now walks the TLV chain; iOS still uses a hard-coded 11-entry show-block table, a `hasPrefix("8301CC03")` ping test and an `E?00E9` substring regex. The builders, palette, wand catalogue, serial and colour-index code match; classification and filtering do not.

I ported both classifiers to Python and ran them over 75 packets (every builder output, all 25 Lab show effects, the Lab experiments, the park captures in docs/PROTOCOL.md §4.1, pings, beacons, wand codes). 39 classify differently. The differences that matter:

- **No channel marker:** any E9 effect directly after `8301` is nil on iOS. That includes the app's own Single/Dual/Rainbow/Circle/Vibrate builds, so the iOS Lab calls its default packet "UNRECOGNISED PACKET" and the default-on iScan filter drops it.
- **Wake prefix:** any effect starting `8301CC03…` is "Interaction Ping" on iOS, unless it is one of the table entries.
- **Wake ping:** `8301CC03000100` is a `show_block` on iOS, so it is filed under Shows and saved to the library. Android never saves pings.
- **Beacon families and ping names:** iOS has no EF05/EF08/E409/E501/EA labels and no "Signal Beacon" / "Show Ping" names.
- **Crash:** `HexUtils.hexToBytes` on iOS has a `precondition` on even length. One odd keystroke in the Lab hex field reaches it.

Missing on iOS altogether: `DisneyTlv` (parser and anatomy), `isShowControl`, `isLibraryNoise`, `rawLabel`/`groupKey`, `BandEffectModel.lightsBand`, `LabPacketBuilder.decode` and `buildRandomShow`, `LabPacketTools`, stacked and user-preset auto-responses, the 16-preset catalogue, and the multi-source scan-record extraction.

`lightsBand` is the piece behind the owner's "only animate what lights the band" request. Android has it as of v1.3.10; the iOS strip still follows every packet.

gaps.title: BandEffectModel.lightsBand and last-light tracking (scan strip follows only packets that light the band)
gaps.androidBehaviour: `BandEffectModel.lightsBand` is true unless kind is NONE, PING or WAND. `handleHeard` computes it for every packet and only then updates `UiState.lastLightHex`, `lastLightLabel` and `lightsHeard`. `LastHeardStrip(hex, lights)` renders `lastLightHex` with title "LAST LIGHTS · #n", or "LAST LIGHTS · NONE HEARD YET". The relay status JSON carries `lastLightHex`, `lastLightLabel`, `lightsHeard`.
gaps.iosState: No `lightsBand`. `LastHeardStrip` takes the newest entry of `vm.livePackets` / `vm.androidLivePackets` whatever its kind and titles it "LAST HEARD · n LIVE", so pings, beacons and wand codes replace the last real effect. The relay status parser reads only `lastHeardHex` / `lastHeardLabel`.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add `var lightsBand: Bool { kind != .none && kind != .ping && kind != .wand }` to `BandEffectModel`. Add `@Published lastLightHex`, `lastLightLabel`, `lightsHeard` to `AppViewModel`, updated in `handlePacket` when `BandEffectModel.from(hex).lightsBand`. Parse `lastLightHex`, `lastLightLabel`, `lightsHeard` from the relay status in `AndroidRemoteClient`. Point `LastHeardStrip` at those fields with the Android titles. In-memory only, no storage.

gaps.title: DisneyTlv parser (parse / Record / Parsed)
gaps.androidBehaviour: `DisneyTlv.parse(hex)` walks `<type><len><value>` records after `8301`. It keeps a cut-short final record with its `declaredLength`, treats `CF 9B` as a legacy Starlight record that consumes the rest, and reports `malformed`. `Parsed` exposes `effect` (first E9), `channel` (zero-length E1..E3), `first(type)`, `has(type)`, `exact`. `Record` exposes `headHex()`, `valueHex()`, `byte(i)`, `isChannelMarker()`, `truncated`. It is the one source of truth for classify, isShowControl, BandEffectModel, withTiming, editableSlots, decode and the Lab anatomy.
gaps.iosState: No DisneyTlv file. Four unrelated substitutes: the regex `E[0-9A-F]00E9` in classify (not byte-aligned, needs a channel marker); a private `records()` walker in BandEffectModel; an inline loop in `LabPacketBuilder.editableSlots`; and `h.range(of: "E9")` in `PacketBuilder.withTiming`. None reports malformed framing and none is shared.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: New `Core/DisneyTlv.swift`: `struct Record { type, value: [UInt8], declaredLength, legacyStarlight }` with `length`, `truncated`, `headHex`, `valueHex`, `byte(_:)`, `isChannelMarker`; `struct Parsed { hex, records, malformed }` with `exact`, `first(_:)`, `has(_:)`, `effect`, `channel`; `static func parse(_:) -> Parsed?`; the `TYPE_*` constants. Port the remain>0 rule for truncated records (DisneyTlv.kt:93-99) exactly. Then make BandEffectModel, editableSlots and withTiming use it.

gaps.title: TLV-based classify(): effect anywhere in the chain, beacon/cue families, ping names, two-entry show-block table
gaps.androidBehaviour: `classifyUncached` order: Starlight; exact match in the 2-entry `showBlocks` ("Lightning", "Rainbow FX"); TLV parse; ping only when there is no E9 record and the first record is CC, named by `DisneyTlv.pingName` ("Signal Beacon", "Wake Ping", "Show Ping (2341)", "Show Ping (2030)", "Interaction Ping"); no E9 goes to `classifyEffectFamily` (EF05 "Color Cue: <colour>" COLOR `fx_ef05`; EF08 "Scene Cue (EF08)" `fx_ef08`; E409 "Show Burst: <colour>" `fx_e409`; E501 "Sync Cue (E501)" `fx_e501`; EA "Animation (style XX)" `fx_ea`; any other leading E0..EF "Effect XXXX" typeInfo `effect`; simKey `FX:<hex>`); otherwise `classifyEffect` on the E9 record with or without channel marker or wake prefix.
gaps.iosState: Order: Starlight; exact match in an 11-entry `showBlocks` (includes the wake ping and 8 packets Android decodes structurally); `hasPrefix("8301CC03")` is always "Interaction Ping"; then the regex `E[0-9A-F]00E9`, nil if absent. No family classification, no ping names. The per-length switch (E905..E914) matches Android once an E9 is found. `extractE905Color` and `extractFadeColor` are dead code, and the "Interaction Ping (Fast Mode)" label is unreachable.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Rewrite `MagicClassifier.classify` lines 15-45 on top of DisneyTlv. Cut `PresetCatalog.showBlocks` to Android's two entries with Android's labels. Add `pingName`. Add `classifyEffectFamily` with the six typeInfos above. Take the E90C/E911 signature windows from the E9 record value, not from "E9 to end of packet". Add Android's length guards on `colors` (e.length >= 5/7/8/6/9). Delete the dead helpers. Switch the iScan filter to `isShowControl` in the same change, or beacons will start passing it.

gaps.title: MagicClassifier.isShowControl (strict show-control filter)
gaps.androidBehaviour: True for `8301CC03…`, any hex containing CF9B/CF0B, any TLV chain with an E9 record, or a show-block hex. It deliberately excludes the EA/EF/E4/E5 beacon families even though they classify. `handleHeard` uses it for the "show control only" filter (pref via `store.getShowControlOnly()`).
gaps.iosState: No equivalent. The iScan filter is `MagicClassifier.classify(hex) == nil` (UserDefaults key `iscan_show_control_only`, default true). It drops every effect without a channel marker and passes any telemetry that happens to contain `E?00E9`.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: `static func isShowControl(_ hexRaw: String) -> Bool` as on Android, and use it at AppViewModel.swift:188 in place of `classify(hex) == nil`.

The store uses it to refuse raw saves, skip on bulk import, count and purge saved band packets, and hide noise in the capture-log analysis (`hideNoise`, default true). `addClassifiedToLibrary` returns "Ping (not saved)" for typeInfo `ping`.

gaps.whatIosNeeds: `static func isLibraryNoise(_:)` with the three prefixes, and an early return in `MagicStore.addClassifiedToLibrary` for typeInfo `ping` ("Ping (not saved)").

Used for raw library labels and the analysed capture-log grouping.

gaps.androidBehaviour: `classify` is wrapped in a synchronized access-ordered LRU of 1024 entries keyed on the raw hex; nil results are cached too.

gaps.title: LabPacketBuilder.decode / Decoded (load a heard packet back into the builder fields)
gaps.androidBehaviour: `decode(hex)` returns `Decoded(type, colors, vibEnabled, vibPattern, rawHex, framing, showIndex)`. It recognises a captured show even when recoloured, by comparing with the colour slots masked to 0. It maps E905 to PRESET, E906 to DUAL, E909 to RAINBOW, E90B to CIRCLE, E908 to RGB (6-bit channels), E911 to CROSSFADE, E912 to ROTATE (reordered to Z1..Z5), a ping to PING and anything else to RAW. gaps.iosState: None. No iOS code references tailVibration, withVibration or toBytes.
