notes:
Method: I read every listed file in full on both sides, then ported both classifiers, `isShowControl` and the BandEffectModel kind logic to Python and ran them over 75 packets. The classify and BandEffectModel examples above are outputs of that port. The three marked "constructed" are not real captures. The resp_vibrate, RANDOM_NEWWAND, preset_t_, any_raw, service-data and hexToBytes rows are read from the code, not executed. Nothing in the repository was edited. The script is at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Magicmaker-mobile/8956e220-2c18-5594-88a6-966886e08e67/scratchpad/drift.py.

On the owner's Android complaint, from the core side only: at HEAD (v1.3.10) `BandEffectModel.lightsBand` is false for every ping-only packet (Signal Beacon, Wake Ping, Show Pings), every EA/EF/E4/E5 beacon family and every wand code in the port. It is true for a wake-prefixed effect (`8301CC03000100E100E9…`), which is a real effect, and for "Single Color: Off". If Android still animates pings or beacons, the cause is a UI consumer rather than the core model. I did not review the Android scan UI.

Order matters when porting: once iOS classify is TLV-based it will start returning non-nil for the EF/EA/E4/E5 families, so the iScan filter must move to `isShowControl` in the same change. iOS `LivePacketSort`, `BleTransmitter.transmitPacket` and the store's dedupe all key on typeInfo, so they pick up the corrected values without edits.

Smaller drift not listed above:
- BandEffectModel timing uses Float on Android and Double on iOS. `durationMs` differs by 1 ms for timing bytes with bit 6 set and count 3, 6, 7, 12 or 14 (0x43 gives 9299 vs 9300). The displayed seconds are the same.
- The iOS `MbleBeaconBuilder.buildPayload` copy right-pads tokens shorter than 28 hex chars where Android left-pads (token "ABCD" gives …ABCD + zeros on iOS, zeros + ABCD on Android). The iOS copy has no caller.
- iOS remote sliders clamp wake preamble to 200...1500 and command burst to 500...5000; Android allows 100..3000 and 500..12000.

iOS-only core items with no Android counterpart, so not gaps: MdeThemeCatalog, MdeLightSequence, PacketBuilder.colorIndex(fromHex:), HexUtils.disneyManufacturerBlock / disneyLeAdvertisingBytes, IScanLivePacket, ScanSessionFile, LabPacketBuilder.ledMasks / isExperimental, NewWandCatalog.randomHex.

Android core/CrashLog.kt and the consumers in data/, service/ and ui/ were read only where needed to judge impact; they belong to other areas.

area: Packet library / data store (Android data/MagicStore.kt, core/MagicModels.kt, relay/CatalogSync.kt, sync/PacketSync.kt vs iOS Data/MagicStore.swift, Core/MagicModels.swift, BLE/AndroidRemoteCatalog.swift)
summary:
iOS has no working local library. A Swift MagicStore exists, but the shipped UI never feeds or reads it: every screen in the tab bar takes its library from the Android catalog pulled over the relay. The only things stored on the iPhone are New Wand names, the wand quick button, a cached copy of the Android catalog, and a 3-column backup scan CSV.

Android features with no reachable iOS counterpart:
- learning heard packets into a library, including raw/unknown packets
- rename, recategorize, unified delete and custom presets
- the band address list and band tagging
- stacked auto rules and creating rules
- capture-log browsing, analysis and add-to-library
- GPS sightings
- library file export/import with a full settings snapshot
- the cloud packets.csv dictionary sync

Where the Swift store does implement the same function, it computes different results: it dedupes per function/colour (Android dedupes per exact hex), saves pings (Android never does), never saves raw packets, seeds a different built-in preset list, and writes an 8-column CSV without comma escaping (Android writes 13 columns, escaped).

One Android bug outside the parity ask is in the notes: the store save throws whenever a recording has no GPS fix.

gaps.title: iPhone-heard packets never reach a local library (local MagicStore is orphaned)
gaps.androidBehaviour: Every heard packet is passed to store.processHeardPacket, which classifies it, learns it into learnedColors / learnedLibrary / learnedRaw and appends it to the session log. The TX tab reads store.allTransmitPackets() (presets + all learned, deduped by canonical hex, presets win), the Wand tab reads store.learnedStarlightPackets(), and the Auto tab reads store.autoRules / customPresets / allLearnedPackets. All of this is local and works with no other device.
gaps.iosState: MagicStore.swift has the same lists and a processHeardPacket, but AppViewModel.handlePacket returns before calling it whenever isLocalListening is true, and that is switched on at launch. The store is only reached when isRecording or isAutoEnabled is set, and only RecordTab / AutoTab set those. RecordTab, AutoTab, PresetsTab, LabTab and FilesTab are compiled into the target but never instantiated: ContentView mounts only RemoteTxView, RemoteWandView, RemoteAutoView, RemoteLabView, RemoteScanTabView and RemoteLinkTabView. Everything the user sees comes from vm.androidCatalog (transmitPresets, wandColors, autoRules), fetched over the relay and cached in UserDefaults key android_catalog_cache_v2 with UNKNOWN/raw rows stripped. With an ESP32 relay and no prior Android sync, the TX and Starlight lists are empty.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Call store.processHeardPacket from the isLocalListening branch of AppViewModel.handlePacket. Add allTransmitPackets(), customPresets, learnedStarlightPackets() and findTransmitPacket(id:) to MagicStore.swift. Give RemoteTxView / RemoteWandView / RemoteAutoView a local data source (MagicPacket rows from the store) and decide the merge rule with androidCatalog; suggested: the local store is authoritative and Android catalog rows are merged in by canonical hex. Delete or re-mount the five dead tab views. The save-path fixes in the 'Save path safety' gap must land with this.

gaps.title: Unknown / raw packets are never learned
gaps.androidBehaviour: hearRawPacket saves every distinct unclassified hex into learnedRaw as MagicPacket{id, hex, label = MagicClassifier.rawLabel(hex), category UNKNOWN, typeInfo "raw", simKey "RAW:<hex>", userRecorded false, rssi}. It dedupes in O(1) through rawHexIndex (a HashSet of canonical hex), caps the list at MAX_RAW_LIBRARY = 20000, skips MagicClassifier.isLibraryNoise (8301C0..., 83010F11..., 8301CC03...) unless the source address is a tagged band (allowNoise), and coalesces saves to one per 2.5 s.
gaps.iosState: hearRawPacket builds a preview packet and always returns added:false with reason "Heard raw (not saved to library)". learnedRaw can only be populated by loading an existing JSON. MagicClassifier.swift has no isLibraryNoise, rawLabel or groupKey.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Port hearRawPacket(hex, rssi, label, allowNoise) with a Set<String> index rebuilt on load and delete, the 20000 cap and a throttled save. Add MagicClassifier.isLibraryNoise and MagicClassifier.rawLabel (24 / 18+4 character rule) to Swift.

gaps.title: Library editing: rename, recategorize (move), unified delete, custom presets
gaps.androidBehaviour: renamePacket(id, newLabel) relabels a row in any of learnedColors / learnedLibrary / learnedRaw / presets; a blank label is ignored. recategorizePacket(id, category) changes only the category field, in place. deletePacketById(id) dispatches to custom preset / colour / library / raw; built-in presets cannot be deleted. saveCustomPreset(label, hex) validates with legacyAdvertiseRejectReason and isDisneyBlePacket, classifies, stores into presets with userRecorded = true (replacing any user preset with the same canonical hex), and also sets lab_hex / lab_label; it returns an error string or null. deleteCustomPreset(id) and the customPresets getter complete the set. UI: the TX tab long-press sheet offers Transmit / Load in Lab / Rename / Recategorize / Delete, the scan promote dialog offers ADD TO TX / RECATEGORIZE, and the Lab has SAVE plus a MY PRESETS list with delete.
gaps.iosState: Locally there is only renameLearnedRaw(id:label:) (raw rows only, never called; a blank label resets to the generated raw label) and deleteLearnedColor / deleteLearnedLibrary / deleteLearnedRaw (called only from the dead PresetsTab). There is no recategorize and no custom presets. Remotely iOS can add a preset on Android (save_custom_preset), delete one wand colour (delete_wand_color) and clear the wand library (clear_wand_library). RelayCommands has no rename, recategorize or delete-packet action, so rows in the iOS TX library are tap-to-send only.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add renamePacket, recategorizePacket, deletePacketById, saveCustomPreset (returning String?), deleteCustomPreset and customPresets to MagicStore.swift. Add a context menu or swipe actions on TX rows (Rename / Recategorize / Load in Lab / Delete). If Android's catalog stays a data source, also add relay actions rename_packet{packetId,label}, recategorize_packet{packetId,category} and delete_packet{packetId} to RelayCommands.kt and its Handlers, and send them from AppViewModel.

gaps.title: My MagicBand address list, band tagging and saved-band cleanup
gaps.androidBehaviour: SharedPreferences "magicmaker" key band_addresses holds a comma-joined list of trimmed, uppercased MACs. bandAddresses(), isBandAddress(), addBandAddress() and removeBandAddress() manage it. Telemetry from a tagged address is whitelisted into learnedRaw (allowNoise). Each Recording carries sourceAddress and isBand, written to the CSV, and tagged rows also go to the band-only sidecar log. savedBandCount() and deleteSavedBands() count and bulk-remove isLibraryNoise rows from learnedRaw. The UI shows the last 8 heard addresses (ServiceState.seenAddresses, max 80, with rssi and count) with TAG / UNTAG, plus manual MAC entry.
gaps.iosState: None. BleCentralDelegate.bleCentral(didReceive:rssi:) carries no source identity (the CBPeripheral is dropped in didDiscover). There is no band_addresses key, Recording has no sourceAddress / isBand, and there is no seen-address list.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Pass peripheral.identifier.uuidString through BleCentral, BleCoordinator.onPacket and AppViewModel.handlePacket into processHeardPacket(address:). Store UserDefaults band_addresses in the same comma-joined format. Add bandAddresses / isBandAddress / addBandAddress / removeBandAddress / savedBandCount / deleteSavedBands to MagicStore.swift, a seen-address list on AppViewModel, and a My MagicBand section in the Scan tab. Caveat: CoreBluetooth never exposes the MAC. The identifier is an iPhone-local UUID that changes when the band rotates its private address, so lists cannot be shared with Android and manual MAC entry has no iOS equivalent.

gaps.title: Auto rules: stacked responses, preset triggers, and creating rules from the iPhone
gaps.androidBehaviour: AutoResponseRule{id, name, triggerPatternId, responsePatternId, responseHex, responseHexes[], enabled}. addAutoRule(name, triggerId, responseIds, responseHexes) stores the whole response stack and defaults to resp_vibrate. findAutoResponses returns List<String>: all stacked hexes, with the RANDOM_NEWWAND token resolved to a fresh New Wand code per fire. Triggers and responses can reference user presets (preset_t_<id>, preset_r_<id>) as well as learned packets. The Auto tab builds the stack from a response picker.
gaps.iosState: The Swift AutoResponseRule has no responseHexes. addAutoRule takes one responseId / responseHex, findAutoResponse returns one hex, and PacketPatterns.swift has no preset_t_ / preset_r_ handling; all of that sits behind the dead AutoTab. The live RemoteAutoView only lists, toggles and deletes Android's rules. iOS never sends add_auto_rule even though Android implements it.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add responseHexes: [String] to the Swift AutoResponseRule (decodeIfPresent, default []). Port addAutoRule(name, triggerId, responseIds, responseHexes), findAutoResponses and resolveResponseHexes, including preset ids and RANDOM_NEWWAND resolution. Add a rule builder (name, trigger picker, response stack) to RemoteAutoView that stores locally and/or sends add_auto_rule{name, triggerPatternId, responsePatternIds[], responseHexes[]}. When firing, send every hex in the stack through the relay in order.

gaps.title: Capture-log management: list, read, delete, analyze, add to library, band and unique sidecars
gaps.androidBehaviour: beginScanSession creates scan_<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.csv (local time) with header timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note,source_address,is_band,lat,lng,accuracy, plus a band-only scan_<stamp>_band.csv with the same header. endScanSession writes scan_<stamp>_unique.csv (hex,count,first_ms,last_ms,label,category,addresses), one row per distinct canonical hex. Fields have commas and newlines replaced by spaces. listLogs() returns LogFile{path, name, sizeBytes, modifiedMs, packetCount} across every storage dir, excluding sidecars. readLog(path) returns LoggedPacket rows. deleteLog(path) removes the log and both sidecars. importHexesToLibrary(hexes) bulk-adds: classified packets go to their proper list, the rest to learnedRaw with userRecorded = true, and it returns the count added. The Logs tab has per-log category / MAC / band-only filters, ANALYZE (group by MagicClassifier.groupKey, hide noise), ADD ALL to LIB, NAME (saveCustomPreset), REPLAY and DELETE.
gaps.iosState: The only log the live UI writes is ISCanBackupLogger: Documents/iscan_backup/iscan_<ISO8601 with ':' replaced by '-'>.csv, header timestamp_ms,hex,rssi, with no label, category or address. MagicStore.swift has beginScanSession / endScanSession / refreshSessions writing an 8-column scan_<ISO8601>.csv into Documents/scan_sessions, but it is unreachable, has no sidecars and does not escape commas. There is no listLogs, readLog, deleteLog or importHexesToLibrary, and no in-app log browser: FilesTab is dead and only lists files with a ShareLink. Logs are reachable only through the Files app.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Use one session logger that writes Android's 13-column header (address / lat / lng blank when unknown), escapes commas, and writes _unique.csv at session end. Add Swift listLogs / readLog / deleteLog / importHexesToLibrary plus MagicClassifier.groupKey. Add a Logs screen (list, filters, analyze, add-all, name, share, delete). The data layer alone is M; with the screen it is L. Timed REPLAY is a broadcast: it would have to go through the relay, and RelayCommands has no sequence or replay action today.

gaps.title: GPS-tagged sightings (lat / lng / accuracy per recording) and the location reader for the map
gaps.androidBehaviour: Recording carries lat, lng (Double, NaN when unknown) and accuracy (Float, -1 when unknown), stamped from the service's last location fix on every heard packet and written to CSV columns 11-13. forEachLoggedLocation streams (lat, lng, rssi, address, label, category) from every chronological log without loading whole files. MapTab uses it for capture points and an RSSI-weighted transmitter estimate per source address.
gaps.iosState: None. Recording has 9 fields with no location or source. CoreLocation is not used anywhere, and Info.plist has no NSLocation usage string.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add a CLLocationManager (when-in-use) and NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription. Add lat / lng / accuracy / sourceAddress / isBand to the Swift Recording as optionals, not NaN: JSONEncoder throws on NaN by default. Write the three CSV columns and add a streaming forEachLoggedLocation. Per-transmitter localisation only works per CoreBluetooth identifier (see the band gap). The map screen itself is outside this area.

gaps.title: Library file export / import and full settings backup
gaps.androidBehaviour: exportLibrary() force-writes /sdcard/MagicMaker/magicmaker_library.json and returns the path. importLibrary() replaces in-memory and internal state from that file, then runs mergeBuiltInPresets and bumps the store revision. Every save mirrors the JSON there when access is granted, and on launch the newer of the internal and external file wins. The JSON is Gson PersistedState{presets, learnedColors, learnedLibrary, learnedRaw?, recordings, autoRules, nextPacketId, nextRecordingId, nextRuleId, starlightSerial, labHex, labLabel, settings, uiSettings}. settings / uiSettings are every key of SharedPreferences "magicmaker" and "magicmaker_ui" as PrefEntry{type: b|i|l|f|s|ss, value, set}, so band addresses, timings, new-wand names, the quick button and relay mode survive a reinstall. UI: a LIBRARY FILE section showing the path with EXPORT / IMPORT.
gaps.iosState: No export or import API or UI. The Swift PersistedState has the same top-level keys minus settings / uiSettings. UserDefaults values (newwand_names_v1, wand_quick_label, wand_quick_hex, android_catalog_cache_v2) are in no backup file. Documents/magicmaker_store.json is already visible and editable in the Files app (UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace are set), but the app reads it only at launch and never offers it for sharing.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add exportLibrary() returning a URL for ShareLink / fileExporter, named magicmaker_library.json. Add importLibrary(from:) via fileImporter that decodes Android's PersistedState and applies it. Make the MagicPacket / Recording / AutoResponseRule decoders tolerant (decodeIfPresent with defaults), because today one missing key fails the whole decode silently through try?. Add settings: [String: PrefEntry] covering the iOS UserDefaults keys. To let Android import an iOS-written file, also write responseHexes on rules and sourceAddress on recordings.

gaps.title: Cloud packet dictionary sync (GitHub packets.csv)
gaps.androidBehaviour: PacketSync reconciles bidirectionally with <BACKUP_REPO>/packets.csv through the GitHub contents API: GET, then PUT with the sha, up to 3 attempts on 409/422. The CSV header is hex,function,category,colors, with quotes around fields containing a comma, quote or newline, sorted by hex. The local side is presets + learnedColors + learnedLibrary with category != UNKNOWN, deduped by canonical hex. Remote-only rows are imported into learnedLibrary as MagicPacket{typeInfo "imported", simKey "", label = function or "Imported"}. Sync runs automatically (throttled to once per 60 s, one at a time) whenever a classified packet is newly learned, and on the SYNC NOW button; the status string is shown in the Logs tab. It is dormant unless BuildConfig.BACKUP_TOKEN and BACKUP_REPO are set at build time.
gaps.iosState: None.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add PacketSync.swift on URLSession (same endpoint, CSV format, throttle and conflict retry). Add cloudSyncConfigured / cloudSync(force:) / cloudKnownEntries / importCloudEntries to MagicStore.swift, and a status line plus SYNC NOW in the UI. Supply the token and repo through xcconfig into Info.plist. A write-scoped GitHub token would then ship inside the IPA, as it already does in the APK; that is an owner decision.

gaps.title: Built-in presets are not merged on upgrade
gaps.androidBehaviour: On every launch with a non-empty store, and after importLibrary, mergeBuiltInPresets() appends any PresetCatalog entry whose hex is not already in presets, giving it a fresh id.
gaps.iosState: prepareIfNeeded seeds presets only when the list is empty. Built-ins added in a later version never appear on an existing install.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Port mergeBuiltInPresets (compare canonical hex) and call it from prepareIfNeeded and from import. Align PresetCatalog.swift with the Android list (see the preset logic-drift entry).

gaps.title: Save path safety: coalesced writes, recordings cap, no save per recording
gaps.androidBehaviour: save() only marks the store dirty; a single background executor coalesces bursts into one write. Raw-learn saves are throttled to one per 2.5 s. recordings is capped at 500 in memory, and persistRecording does not call save() because the CSV is the durable record. saveLabHex / saveLabLabel write prefs only. updateLearnedColor saves only when the row actually changed.
gaps.iosState: save() JSON-encodes the entire state on the main actor on every call; only the file write is off-main. persistRecording inserts into an unbounded recordings array and calls save() for every packet. saveLabHex and saveLabLabel each call save(). updateLearnedColor calls save() on every repeat of a wand broadcast.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Add a dirty flag with a debounced encode off the main actor. Cap recordings at 500 and remove save() from persistRecording and the lab setters. Add an equality guard in updateLearnedColor. Harmless today because the store is unreachable; required as soon as the store is wired to the live scan.

gaps.title: Lab scratch state is not persisted (lab_hex / lab_label), no label or TAG in the live Lab
gaps.androidBehaviour: lab_hex and lab_label live in SharedPreferences, are restored when the Lab opens and are included in PersistedState. loadIntoLab(hex, label) is called from other tabs. applyLabLabelToMatchingRaw (the TAG button) relabels the learnedRaw row whose canonical hex equals the lab hex. SAVE calls saveCustomPreset(label, hex).
gaps.iosState: The live Lab binds to vm.androidLabHex, an in-memory @Published string that starts empty and is set to the wake ping after a catalog apply. It is lost on relaunch, and the live Lab has no label field, SAVE or TAG. MagicStore.swift has getLabHex / getLabLabel / saveLabHex / saveLabLabel / loadIntoLab / applyLabLabelToMatchingRaw, but only the dead LabTab and PresetsTab call them.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Initialise androidLabHex from store.getLabHex() and write it back through saveLabHex (prefs only). Add a label field with SAVE (saveCustomPreset) and TAG (applyLabLabelToMatchingRaw) to RemoteLabView.

gaps.title: Relay TX power and interleave mode cannot be set from the iPhone
gaps.androidBehaviour: MagicStore persists tx_power_level (0..3 = ULTRA_LOW / LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH, default 3) and tx_interleave (Boolean, default false), read by BleAdvertiser and MagicTransmitter and edited in the Lab transmission settings.
gaps.iosState: iOS remote-controls wake preamble, command burst and starlight burst only. RelayCommands has no action for power or interleave, and neither value appears in statusJson or the catalog.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Android side: add relay actions set_tx_power{level} and set_tx_interleave{enabled}, and expose both values in statusJson. iOS side: two AppViewModel methods and two controls in the TRANSMISSION SETTINGS disclosure group.

gaps.title: Loop packet lookup for TX / Starlight loops (findTransmitPacket, findLearnedStarlight)
gaps.androidBehaviour: findTransmitPacket(id) and findLearnedStarlight(id) (the latter also resolves New Wand ids >= 1,000,000 through NewWandCatalog.byId) give the foreground service the hex and label for the repeating TX loop and wand loop.
gaps.iosState: iOS passes packetId and intervalMs to the relay (set_tx_loop, set_starlight_loop) and shows the loop label from the status.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing on iOS.
gaps.notApplicableReason: The loops are executed by the broadcasting device's foreground service (needs BLE advertising); iOS only selects the packet id over the relay.

gaps.title: Relay catalog server side: CatalogSync chunker, relay cache refresh, storeRevision bump
gaps.androidBehaviour: CatalogSync splits the catalog (tx / wand / rules) into chunks of at most 460 bytes for the GATT STATUS characteristic. MagicStore calls MagicMakerForegroundService.refreshRelayCache after rule edits and ServiceState.bumpStoreRevision after every library edit, so a connected iPhone re-pulls.
gaps.iosState: The client half exists: CatalogChunkSync speaks protocol 1 (catalog_sync_begin / catalog_sync_chunk), and AppViewModel re-fetches when status.storeRevision changes.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing on iOS, apart from the BLE field loss in the logic-drift list, which is fixed on the Android side or by iOS re-deriving the fields.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Exists only to make Android a relay host (GATT / HTTP server side); iOS is the client.

gaps.title: Shared-storage locations: All-files access, /sdcard/MagicMaker, multi-directory log discovery
gaps.androidBehaviour: With MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE granted, the library mirrors to /sdcard/MagicMaker/magicmaker_library.json and logs go to /sdcard/MagicMaker/logs. allLogDirs() also scans the app external-files and internal scan_sessions dirs so older captures stay listed. externalAuthoritative prevents overwriting an SD library that has not been read yet.
gaps.iosState: A single sandbox location (Documents), already exposed in the Files app through UIFileSharingEnabled and LSSupportsOpeningDocumentsInPlace.
gaps.whatIosNeeds: Nothing; the user-facing equivalent is the document-picker export/import in the library file gap.
gaps.notApplicableReason: Android-only OS facility (all-files access / removable shared storage); iOS has one sandboxed Documents directory, already visible in Files.

iosAlreadyAtParity: MagicCategory values and wire strings (SHOW / ANIMATION / COLOR / UNKNOWN) and the category-to-list mapping in packetsFor / packets(for:) are identical (MagicModels.kt:3, MagicStore.kt:336-343 vs MagicModels.swift:3-8, MagicStore.swift:111-118).
MagicPacket schema is field-for-field identical (id, hex, label, category, typeInfo, colors, simKey, userRecorded, rssi?, wandVerified) (MagicModels.kt:5-16 vs MagicModels.swift:10-21).

Internal store file name and base JSON shape match: magicmaker_store.json with presets, learnedColors, learnedLibrary, learnedRaw?, recordings, autoRules, nextPacketId, nextRecordingId, nextRuleId, starlightSerial, labHex, labLabel. iOS lacks only settings / uiSettings.

New Wand catalog is generated identically on both sides: prefix 8301CF0B00C020224EAC7807866, range E80..FFF minus F20..F7F, ids 1,000,000 + offset, typeInfo newwand, simKey NEWWAND:<hex> (NewWandCatalog.kt:12-43 vs LabPacketBuilder.swift:358-387).

New Wand custom names work on-device on both: long-press rename, keyed by uppercased hex, blank clears. Storage differs: Android stores prefs "magicmaker" key newwand_names as a JSON-object string; iOS stores UserDefaults newwand_names_v1 as a [String:String] dictionary. Default row text also differs: Android shows the last 4 hex chars plus the colour name, iOS shows "New Wand E80" plus the full hex (MagicMakerScreens.kt:1640-1657, 1693-1699 vs AppViewModel.swift:86-107, RemoteTab.swift:606-671).
Wand quick button: same keys (wand_quick_label, wand_quick_hex) and same default hex 8301CF0B00C020224EAC7807866F1D (MagicMakerScreens.kt:1385-1386, 1637 vs AppViewModel.swift:110-120).
Starlight serial capture into starlight_serial when a full wand packet is heard is the same code path (MagicStore.kt:867-874 vs MagicStore.swift:312-318), though unreachable on iOS today.
HexUtils.canonicalHex and isDisneyBlePacket, the gate for processHeardPacket, are identical (HexUtils.kt:21-37 vs HexUtils.swift:23-49).

Remote control of Android's library that already exists on iOS: add custom preset, delete wand colour, clear wand library, toggle and delete auto rules, and the wake-preamble / command-burst / starlight-burst timings (AppViewModel.swift:722-836).

The synced Android catalog is cached across launches (UserDefaults android_catalog_cache_v2, JSON of {catalog, revision}), so an ESP32-only session can reuse the last Android library (AppViewModel.swift:568-603).

A show-control-only scan filter preference exists on both: Android pref show_control_only, iOS UserDefaults iscan_show_control_only. The filter predicate itself differs and belongs to the classifier area.

logicDrift.what: Unclassified (raw) packet: learned or not
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301AA0211223344 heard with the show-control filter off
logicDrift.androidResult: A new learnedRaw row {label "Raw: 8301AA0211223344", category UNKNOWN, typeInfo raw, simKey RAW:8301AA0211223344}; RecordEvent(added=true, "Learned raw -> Unknown").
logicDrift.iosResult: Nothing stored; RecordEvent(added=false, "Heard raw (not saved to library)").

logicDrift.what: Pings: Android never stores them, iOS stores them as Shows
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301CC03000000 (beacon ping) and 8301CC03000100 (wake ping)
logicDrift.androidResult: Both classify as typeInfo ping and addClassifiedToLibrary returns added=false "Ping (not saved)"; the library is unchanged.
logicDrift.iosResult: 8301CC03000000 is added to learnedLibrary as "Interaction Ping" (dedupe key FUNC:ping, so one ping row that later pings overwrite). 8301CC03000100 matches the iOS-only show block "Show: Wakeup Ping" and is added to learnedLibrary as a show_block.

logicDrift.what: Show / animation dedupe: Android per exact hex, iOS per function family (later packets overwrite the stored hex)
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301E100E90F00520EF57AEC5C021902190248ABB0 then 8301E100E90F00520EE27AEC5C021902190248ABB0 (same E90F effect, centre colour Red vs Blue)
logicDrift.androidResult: Two learnedLibrary rows, both labelled "Centre Pulse (E90F)", each keeping its own hex.
logicDrift.iosResult: One row. libraryDedupeKey is FUNC:e90f for both, so the second packet returns "Verified ..." and overwrites the stored hex and label; the Red variant is lost.

logicDrift.what: Single / dual colour dedupe: Android per exact hex, iOS per colour simKey
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301E100E90500090E15B0 then 8301CC03000100E100E90500090E15B0 (same red, without and with the wake-ping prefix)
logicDrift.androidResult: Two learnedColors rows ("Single Color: Red" twice, with different hex).
logicDrift.iosResult: One row; the second returns added=false "Verified Red" because the key is C1:15.

logicDrift.what: Starlight wand dedupe, truncated-packet guard and reason text
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301CF9B00AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA15 then 8301CF9B00BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB15 (two wands, same colour 0x15); also the truncated 8301CF9B0015
logicDrift.androidResult: Two learnedColors rows (dedupe by exact stored hex among typeInfo starlight), reason "Learned Red -> Wand"; the Wand tab collapses by colour only at display time. The truncated packet is rejected: starlightLearnColorIndex is null, so "Heard Red (unrecognized wand format)" and nothing is saved.
logicDrift.iosResult: One row keyed SL:15. The second wand overwrites the stored hex (and serial), reason "Learned Red -> Colors" on first sight. The truncated packet is saved as a learned colour because there is no learn-index guard.

logicDrift.what: Built-in preset seed list, and which list a known packet lands in
logicDrift.exampleInput: Fresh install; then hearing 8301CC03000100E100E90500090E02B0
logicDrift.androidResult: 16 presets from PresetCatalog.all (Ping, Vibrate band, Vibrate (rainbow FX), 8 colours, Dual YO/Blue, 5-LED Rainbow, Circle, Crossfade R/B, Lightning), ids 1..16, simKey "P:<label>", typeInfo = kind name. The heard packet classifies as "Single Color: Blue" (COLOR) and is added to learnedColors.
logicDrift.iosResult: 11 presets derived from showBlocks ("Show: Wakeup Ping", "Show: Ambient Blue", ..., "Show: Fast Sparkle"), all category show with simKey SHOW:<hex>; the six animationPresets collapse into them because they share hex. The heard packet matches show block "Show: Ambient Blue" (SHOW) and is added to learnedLibrary.

logicDrift.what: Session CSV: columns, escaping and file name
logicDrift.exampleInput: An E913 packet such as 8301E100E913000F0EBBB5A200000000000000000000000000 (colors string "White centre, Blue / Red")
logicDrift.androidResult: A 13-column row under timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note,source_address,is_band,lat,lng,accuracy; the comma in colors is replaced by a space. File scan_<yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH-mm-ss>.csv in local time, plus _band.csv and _unique.csv sidecars.
logicDrift.iosResult: A row with 9 comma-separated fields under an 8-column header (timestamp_ms,hex,rssi,label,category,type_info,colors,note), so note shifts one column. logicDrift.what: Auto-response resolution on iOS iScan auto vs Android (stack, RANDOM_NEWWAND token, learned / preset triggers)

logicDrift.iosResult: maybeIscanAutoRespond sends only responseHexes.first, verbatim: the literal "RANDOM_NEWWAND" goes through HexUtils.canonicalHex and is transmitted as "8301ADEAD", and the second packet is never sent. learned_t_ / preset_t_ triggers never match because the matcher is called with learned: [].

logicDrift.what: Catalog rows lose colors / userRecorded / wandVerified over BLE chunked sync but keep them over WiFi

logicDrift.iosResult: Over WiFi the subtitle is "Red - LEARNED - WAND OK". Over BLE, AndroidRemotePreset.parse defaults colors to "" and both flags to false, so the subtitle is empty; simKey is sent but iOS has no field for it and drops it.

logicDrift.what: Generated raw label truncation threshold

logicDrift.what: In-memory recordings list and persistence per recorded packet

ANDROID BUG OUTSIDE THE PARITY ASK. buildState() puts recordings into the JSON (A:232-238). Recording.lat / lng default to Double.NaN (MagicModels.kt:39-40), and the service passes NaN whenever there is no location fix (MagicMakerForegroundService.kt:1072-1073). MagicStore builds Gson with GsonBuilder().create() (A:23), which refuses NaN. I reproduced this with a 10-line Java program against the gson-2.10 jar in the local Gradle install (the app pins 2.10.1): toJson throws IllegalArgumentException "NaN is not a valid double value". So once one no-fix recording is in memory, saveNow() throws on every save (caught and sent to CrashLog at A:285) and exportLibrary() returns null, so library edits made in that process are not persisted. I did not run the Android app; the serializer behaviour is what was verified. INFERRED, NOT RUN. An iOS-written store JSON imported on Android would leave AutoResponseRule.responseHexes null, because Gson does not apply Kotlin defaults for classes without a no-arg constructor, and PacketPatterns.kt:111 would then throw. This is why the export gap asks iOS to write that field.

OUT OF AREA. The classifiers differ (Android walks TLV records and has EF / E4 / EA families and 2 show blocks; iOS uses an E?00E9 regex and 11 show blocks). That changes what each store would learn and is left to the classifier area, apart from the store-level examples in logicDrift.

area: TX, WAND, AUTO and LAB screens (excluding the radio broadcast itself)
summary: The four iOS screens (RemoteTxView / RemoteWandView / RemoteAutoView / RemoteLabView in Views/RemoteTab.swift) are remote controls for an Android phone, not a port of the Android screens. The Lab packet builder is the only part at near parity and it works offline. Everything that is library management on Android (TX list, rename, recategorize, delete, save-from-Lab, My Presets, labels/TAG, auto-rule creation, learned wand colours) is missing on iOS or only reachable through an Android relay, because iOS has no library of its own on any reachable code path: its lists are the cached Android catalogue, and the iPhone's own scan never writes to the local MagicStore. With an ESP32 relay (which per firmware only acts on transmit / keep_awake / vibrate and acks everything else) TX loop, Wand loop, Interrogate, timing, auto-rule edits and MBLE are silent no-ops that still report success. Lab is missing decode-into-builder, Packet Anatomy, Packet Inspector (byte grid + vibration stepper), Random Light Show, SAVE/TAG/LABEL and My Presets. Two iOS bugs found while comparing: (1) the Lab hex field crashes the app on any odd number of hex digits (precondition in HexUtils.hexToBytes; Android deliberately tolerates it); (2) the iOS classifier does not recognise the builder's own default packets (no channel marker), so the Lab summary card says UNRECOGNISED PACKET for Single/Dual/Rainbow/Circle/Vibrate until the channel-marker toggle is on.

logicDrift.what: Hex with an odd number of digits (the normal state while hand-editing the Lab hex field). Android's hexToBytes drops the trailing nibble on purpose; iOS's has precondition(clean.count % 2 == 0), and it is reached on every Lab render via BandPreviewView -> BandEffectModel.from, LabBuilderPanel.summaryCard (legacyAdvertiseRejectReason and hexToBytes(hex).count), LabPacketBuilder.editableSlots and the SEND button's disabled expression.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Delete the last character of the Lab hex field: 8301E905002E0EE0B (17 digits)
logicDrift.androidResult: Parsed as 8 bytes; preview/summary update; no crash (comment: 'callers run on every keystroke and must not crash').
logicDrift.iosResult: precondition failure 'Invalid hex length' -> the app terminates (precondition is active in release builds).

logicDrift.what: Lab summary card ('YOU ARE BUILDING') for effect packets without a channel marker. Android classifies by walking TLV records; iOS requires the regex E[0-9A-F]00E9, so the builder's own defaults for Single / Dual / Rainbow / Circle / Vibrate (defaultFraming has channelMarker=false) are not recognised, and a wake-prefixed packet without a channel marker is called a ping.
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301E905002E0EE0B0 (Lab default Single Color: Cyan); 8301CC03000100E905002E0EE0B0 (same with 'Wake ping first')
logicDrift.androidResult: 'SINGLE COLOR: CYAN' in cyan with colours 'CYAN' for both.
logicDrift.iosResult: First: classify returns nil -> 'UNRECOGNISED PACKET' in amber. Second: 'INTERACTION PING'.

logicDrift.what: Show-block table differs (Android PresetCatalog.showBlocks has 2 entries, iOS has 11 including the wake ping and the ambient colours), and it is consulted before any other rule on both platforms, so the same Park Show / ping gets a different label, typeInfo and colours in the Lab summary.
logicDrift.exampleInput: 8301CC03000100E100E90500090E02B0 (Lab Park Show 'Ambient Blue'); 8301CC03000100 (Wake Ping type)
logicDrift.androidResult: 'Single Color: Blue', typeInfo single, colours 'Blue'; ping -> 'Wake Ping', typeInfo ping.
logicDrift.iosResult: 'Show: Ambient Blue', typeInfo show_block, no colours; ping -> 'Show: Wakeup Ping', typeInfo show_block.

logicDrift.what: Summary-card detail line: Android reads framing/buzz/validity from the packet itself; iOS prints the builder's toggle state and only for types where framing/vibration apply.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Park Show 'Lightning' 8301CC03000100E100E90C000F0F5D465BF00532374895; truncated raw 8301E905002E
logicDrift.androidResult: 'WAKE PING FIRST · CHANNEL 1 · 23 BYTES · FITS IN BLE'; the truncated packet shows 'MALFORMED' with a red border.
logicDrift.iosResult: '23 BYTES · FITS IN BLE' only; the truncated packet shows 'UNRECOGNISED PACKET' in amber with no malformed flag.

logicDrift.what: Auto rule whose response is 'New Wand: RANDOM code'. Android stores the token RANDOM_NEWWAND in responseHexes and resolves it to a fresh code on every fire. The iPhone-scan auto path transmits rule.responseHexes.first verbatim, and canonicalHex keeps only the hex letters of the token.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Rule from the Android catalogue with responseHexes ["RANDOM_NEWWAND"], fired by iPhone scan auto-response
logicDrift.androidResult: Transmits a random code from NewWandCatalog, e.g. 8301CF0B00C020224EAC7807866E93.
logicDrift.iosResult: Sends transmit hex '8301ADEAD' (the letters A,D,E,A,D of the token) to the relay.

logicDrift.what: Stacked auto responses.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Rule with responseHexes [8301CC03000100, 8301E905002E0EFBB5]
logicDrift.androidResult: Sends both in order (findAutoResponses returns the list; transmitter.sendSequence).
logicDrift.iosResult: iPhone-scan auto sends only the first hex.

logicDrift.what: Rules triggered by a specific library packet. Android resolves preset_t_<id> (simKey or exact hex) and learned_t_<id> (simKey) against its store. iOS has no preset_t_ handling and calls matchesTriggerId with learned: [], so neither kind can match.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Rule with triggerPatternId preset_t_17 or learned_t_45, matching packet heard by the iPhone
logicDrift.androidResult: Rule fires.
logicDrift.iosResult: Never fires (matchesTriggerId returns false).

logicDrift.what: System response 'Vibrate band' (resp_vibrate) default hex.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Rule with responsePatternId resp_vibrate and empty responseHexes
logicDrift.androidResult: 8301E905002E0EFBB5 (white preset + burst vibration, PacketBuilder.vibrateBand()).
logicDrift.iosResult: 8301CC03000100E100E90C000F0F5D465BF005323748B0 (the rainbow finale; PresetCatalog.vibratePacket).

logicDrift.what: Timing slider ranges and placeholder defaults.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Android COMMAND BURST set to 8000 ms (allowed 500..12000, default 4000); WAKE SLICE 2000 ms (allowed 100..3000)
logicDrift.androidResult: Shows and keeps 8000 / 2000.
logicDrift.iosResult: Sliders are 500...5000 and 200...1500, so they pin at 5000 / 1500 and any commit sends the clamped value back to Android; before the first sync iOS assumes 2000 ms command burst.

logicDrift.what: TX library after an offline relaunch: the iOS cache drops every preset with category UNKNOWN or typeInfo raw, which includes user presets saved from an unclassified hex (Android stores those as UNKNOWN/raw with userRecorded=true).
logicDrift.exampleInput: Custom preset saved on Android from a hex the classifier does not recognise, e.g. 8301C10203
logicDrift.androidResult: Listed under UNKNOWN in TX and under MY PRESETS.
logicDrift.iosResult: Visible right after a sync, gone from the TX list after relaunching without a relay.

logicDrift.what: Wand footer in New Wand mode.
logicDrift.exampleInput: WAND tab, NEW WAND selected, Android library holding 5 learned Starlight colours
logicDrift.androidResult: 'LIB 288' (the generated code count) and no CLR LIB button.
logicDrift.iosResult: 'LIB 5' and an enabled 'Clr Lib' that wipes the Android Starlight library with no confirmation.

logicDrift.what: Order of rows inside a TX section.
logicDrift.exampleInput: Labels 'Zebra' and 'blue test' in the same section
logicDrift.androidResult: Zebra, blue test (sortedBy label, ordinal).
logicDrift.iosResult: blue test, Zebra (localizedCaseInsensitiveCompare).
